# Development verification

## Verification schedule

Tests declare every milestone whose requirements they directly verify. Incidental
use of a capability does not establish coverage. Use module markers for uniform
coverage and function or parameter markers for mixed modules. Registered markers
are `milestone_0` through `milestone_6`, `milestone_50`, `milestone_99`, and
`infrastructure` for contributor tooling without direct milestone requirements.
Collection fails with test IDs when any case lacks classification, even if a
selector would exclude it. Multiple selected associations execute a case once.

```sh
# Implementation phase gate: substitute the current milestone
uv run --locked pytest -n 4 --dist=loadgroup -m milestone_1

# Story acceptance for any milestone, and default local selection: M1–6
uv run --locked pytest -n 4 --dist=loadgroup

# Complete suite: explicit developer command or CI
uv run --locked pytest -n 4 --dist=loadgroup -m ""
```

The default expression is `milestone_1 or milestone_2 or milestone_3 or
milestone_4 or milestone_5 or milestone_6`. A phase gate selects only its current
milestone; it does not automatically select earlier milestones. Every story
acceptance selects M1–6, including stories in M0 and M50. Other local pytest
selections and standalone artifact drivers require an explicit developer command.
Selected tests may invoke artifact drivers internally. CI keeps the complete
suite and its existing standalone artifact verification. Preserve assertions,
timeouts, xdist groups and the three documented temporary skips.

## Local parallel test execution

Agents must use four workers with `loadgroup` for local pytest verification,
including complete-suite runs and selected tests. After locked development
synchronization, use:

```sh
uv run --locked pytest -n 4 --dist=loadgroup
uv run --locked pytest -n 4 --dist=loadgroup --junitxml=/private/tmp/agentic-ml-parallel.xml --durations=20
```

For serial diagnosis or a short focused TDD cycle, use `uv run --locked pytest`
with the relevant selector and record why serial execution was selected.
Use two workers only for an explicit comparison or resource investigation.
Pytest configuration does not add worker flags automatically; local and CI test
commands explicitly select four workers with `loadgroup`.

`pytest-xdist` is a development dependency. Pytest is constrained to `>=8,<9.2`
because pytest 9.2.0 silently breaks group scheduling with pytest-xdist 3.8.0.
The public subprocess regression in `test_parallel_execution.py` verifies that
marked cases share a worker. Revisit the upper bound after an upstream-compatible
pair passes that regression and complete-suite verification.

`loadgroup` keeps the installation
tests in one worker and the distribution tests in another scheduling group;
each group runs sequentially, but a worker can run other tests afterward.
Initialization and CLI cases are ungrouped and can run individually on available
workers. Grouping does not guarantee test order. Use `loadgroup` with these
commands so shared mutable installation fixtures stay together and expensive
distribution fixtures are reused. Avoid `loadfile`/`loadscope`: they place the
entire initialization module on one worker.

Each worker creates its own module fixtures. Experiment projects, source Git
fixtures, databases, storage and artifact directories use explicitly owned pytest
temporary paths. Installation probes intentionally
mutate their group-local installed project and restore its contents. Cache-removal
checks remove only their own workspace cache. Keep those isolation properties
when adding tests. Do not point multiple runs at the same `--basetemp` directory.

A scoped hardlink experiment was rolled back after its full-suite runtime
regressed. Fixtures again use their prior installation configuration, including
the installation-verification driver's copy mode and private cache for mutation
tests. The [experiment report](../verification/pytest-hardlink-fixtures.md) preserves
the measurements and a replayable candidate patch; its hardlink policy is not
active.

Environment installation and MLflow initialization compete for CPU, memory and
disk. Investigate resource constraints with a recorded worker-count comparison. Keep
existing assertions and subprocess timeouts intact. Record worker count, suite
count, durations, diagnostics and platform with results. A parallel run with `-m ""` exercises the full suite; broader local runs require an explicit developer command. Retain serial execution for diagnosis. Parallel macOS evidence
does not establish Linux or Windows support. The Linux CI workflow now requests
four workers; hosted parallel verification remains pending until a run is observed.

The initial verified macOS benchmark passed 129 tests in 16m59s with two workers
and 12m06s with four. Four workers reduced elapsed time by about 29%, while some
individual tests took longer under contention. These measurements are not a
Linux performance claim. See [parallel verification](../verification/parallel-test-execution.md)
for grouping checks, compatibility findings, commands and retained evidence.


## Pytest workspace ownership and retention

Repository `tests/conftest.py` loads contributor workspace support. Tests that
request `tmp_path` receive an exclusive root. Pass a fresh child to verification
drivers, for example `--workspace str(tmp_path / "verification")`; let the driver
create that child. Composed drivers pass fresh descendants to their children.
Standalone default allocation is tested with a controlled `TMPDIR` beneath the
owning test root, an unrelated cwd and pytest context removed.

By default, a successful test's entire owned tree is removed after every fixture
finalizer has finished, before its completed teardown report is delivered. This
includes nested workspaces and driver-retained environments. Setup, call and
teardown failures preserve available diagnostics and report
`WORKSPACE <absolute-path>`. A cleanup error fails teardown and reports the
remaining path. Original test failures remain visible.

Shared fixtures use `owned_workspace(request, tmp_path_factory, name)` from
`pytest_workspace_support` at their existing scope. Their paths remain available
until the last consumer and fixture finalizer finish. Failed consumers or shared
finalizers retain the available tree. A direct `tmp_path_factory.mktemp` allocation
does not register this ownership; use the helper for maintained shared fixtures.
Keep existing fixture scopes, mutable-probe restoration and scheduling groups.

Default numbered-session retention is one completed invocation:
`tmp_path_retention_count = 1`, requested policy `failed`. A failed tree survives
its invocation and is eligible for eviction when the next numbered invocation
completes. Native pytest session locks protect active invocations. Empty session
containers may remain to advance numbered retention even though successful test
trees are already gone. The support routes native container retention separately
from test-tree retention; effective native configuration can therefore show `all`.
Its public `Config.inicfg` compatibility mapping is deprecated in locked pytest
9.1.1; revisit that routing before a toolchain upgrade. The
[US-36 IP1 report](../verification/us-36-ip1.md) records the reason and limits.

| Retention control | Effect |
|---|---|
| No override | Remove successful test/shared trees during teardown; retain failures for one numbered invocation |
| `-o tmp_path_retention_policy=all` | Retain successful trees within ordinary numbered-session retention |
| `--keep-test-workspaces` | Retain test/shared trees; without an explicit base, use a unique unnumbered root outside later numbered-session eviction |
| Driver `--keep-workspace` | Retain driver environments for remaining test consumers; outer pytest cleanup still applies |

To inspect successful pytest workspaces, run, for example:

```sh
uv run --locked pytest -n 4 --dist=loadgroup -m milestone_0 --keep-test-workspaces tests/integration/test_distribution_verification.py
```

An explicit `--basetemp` must name a new, exclusively owned directory. Existing
bases, symlinks and overlap with the harness checkout or durable records are
rejected before pytest clears files. Explicit bases do not have numbered-session
eviction semantics. Retained explicit bases and `--keep-test-workspaces` roots
need deliberate contributor cleanup; subsequent invocations must use new paths.

Use a dedicated child base for nested pytest, such as
`tmp_path / "nested-pytest"`. Never supply an active parent's or sibling's base.
Workers, independent sessions and nested runs must not share workspace roots.
Interrupted runs may leave incomplete trees and records; forced termination cannot
guarantee fixture finalizers or cleanup. Preserve available diagnostics when
investigating them. These lifecycle rules do not change standalone driver
cleanup, which preserves source/project files after removing owned environments.

Raw verification records belong in checkout `.dev-records/verification/`, outside
disposable pytest paths. Never use that directory as a temporary base. Follow the
[records policy](records.md) for lifetime retention and backups.

## Phase and story verification

This policy governs local verification, including unfinished work in approved plans.
Record revisions to those plans through [manage-plan-scope](../../.agents/skills/manage-plan-scope/SKILL.md).
Preserve completed evidence and approvals. CI continues running all tests.

### Implementation phase gates

Use TDD for new behavior and bug fixes, with focused public-interface checks for
red–green cycles. At each executable phase gate, run the entire current milestone
using `uv run --locked pytest -n 4 --dist=loadgroup -m milestone_N` (substitute N).
Focused checks do not replace that selection. Preserve developer approval gates.

Record changed modules, confirmed public boundaries, applicable acceptance
criteria, exact commands, collected/selected/deselected counts, outcomes and
platform. Preserve assertions, timeouts and known failures. Identify excluded
coverage and its owning task; excluded tests and skips do not prove acceptance.
Documentation-only phases use document/link/whitespace checks with a rationale.

Retain locked synchronization, lock consistency, lint, formatting, strict typing,
CLI version smoke and `git diff --check`. Record the lock hash before and after.

### Story acceptance

For every milestone, run `uv run --locked pytest -n 4 --dist=loadgroup` against
final story changes: M1–6 only. Renew that evidence after executable changes.
Reconcile acceptance criteria, excluded coverage, temporary skips and unresolved
failures. Retain shared checks and explicit developer story acceptance. Broader
pytest runs and standalone artifact checks require the developer's explicit
command; they are not automatic acceptance requirements. Documentation-only
stories use appropriate document checks with a rationale.

### Milestone acceptance

Keep a named milestone verification owner to reconcile historical deferrals,
known failures, evidence identities, counts and platform/manual limitations.
Milestone acceptance does not automatically trigger a local full suite or
standalone artifact drivers. Broader verification requires the developer's
explicit command. Preserve historical approvals and evidence without treating
excluded coverage or CI results as proof of a local check.

## Scheduling policy revision — 2026-11-04

The developer's supplied “Stratify tests by milestone” plan explicitly authorizes
this replacement of phase/story scheduling and revision of unfinished M1/M50
verification obligations. Owning plans record the scope changes. Historical
results, approvals, unresolved failures and the three temporary skips remain.
"}

# Architecture Decisions

Part of the [harness design](../agentic-ml-harness-design.md). Scope: Architecture Decision Records.

**Related contracts:** Read [interfaces and configuration](interfaces-and-configuration.md); [execution and governance](execution-and-governance.md); [data and features](data-and-features.md); [milestone delivery](milestone-delivery.md) when changing behavior that crosses these boundaries. Consult the [reading map and authority rules](../agentic-ml-harness-design.md#reading-map-and-document-authority) and [architecture decisions](architecture-decisions.md) before implementation.

## 14. Architecture Decision Records

### ADR-001 — Hierarchical Closed-Loop ML Development

**Status: Accepted**

**Decision:** The harness will implement a model-improvement inner loop and data-improvement outer loop. The orchestrator coordinates both, while the harness executes and independently validates actions. Developers approve workflow phase boundaries and acquisition scope changes.

**Rationale:** Poor model performance can reflect insufficient or unrepresentative data, not just inadequate features, architecture, or hyperparameters. Feedback must support both model and dataset improvement.

**Consequences:** Requires data-gap diagnostics, acquisition contracts, dataset versioning, authorization, consistent before/after evaluation, and termination conditions for both loops.

### ADR-007 — GitHub Package Installation and Project Initialization

**Status: Installation decisions accepted; remaining interface details pending**

**Decision:** Initially install the harness as a normal Python package directly from its GitHub repository using `uv`, pinned to a full commit SHA. Use `agentic-ml` as the installed CLI name and retain `agentic_ml` as the Python import name. Users install `uv` and Git, initialize a separate Git/Python project, install the harness into that project's environment, and then run `uv run agentic-ml init`. No separate initializer-tool installation is required. Package-registry distribution is future work.

**CLI naming correction (2026-10-29):** The developer corrected the original CLI spelling to `agentic-ml`, matching the distribution name; the Python import remains `agentic_ml`. This supersedes the earlier `agent-ml` spelling in issue bodies and historical reviews/evidence. Update current entrypoints, tests, guidance, and acceptance-criterion wording without changing criterion IDs or capability scope. No legacy alias is required for this initial implementation.

**Rationale:** Direct GitHub installation supports the separate-repository workflow without requiring package-registry publishing. A full commit pin identifies the exact harness source used by an experiment.

**Consequences:** The repository must build an installable package containing the CLI, templates, and runtime guidance. The initializer preserves existing project files and the pinned dependency. Run provenance records the harness repository URL, full commit SHA, package version, and project lockfile identity. Users need GitHub access at installation/restoration time; the installer may fetch source into its cache, but runtime use requires no manually maintained harness checkout.

**Installation source/name resolution (2026-10-30):** The accepted US-31 plan and implemented package metadata establish `https://github.com/jimthompson5802/agentic-ml.git` and distribution `agentic-ml`; these are settled implementation inputs for US-01. Full-SHA installation verification is recorded in [US-01 IP1 evidence](../../verification/us-01-ip1.md).

**Remaining decisions:** Additional Python versions to verify beyond the required Python 3.12 baseline, API compatibility/versioning policy, project/experiment configuration schemas, and CLI/API details beyond `agentic-ml init`.

**Milestone 0 scope clarification (2026-10-29):** Development and testing may install the package from the harness repository. Publishing to PyPI or another package registry is not required. Milestone 0 demonstrates a minimal package: `agentic-ml --version`, `agentic_ml` imports, provisional template and runtime guidance resources, wheel/source-distribution builds, and isolated verification of both the directly built wheel and a wheel rebuilt from the source distribution. This preserves US-31–US-33's acceptance criteria; full-commit-pinned GitHub installation and usable experiment initialization remain Milestone 1 work.

Python 3.12 is the required initial verification baseline; additional verified versions may remain pending. Record the distribution name and repository installation source in the Milestone 0 implementation plan before dependent package configuration. The distribution name `agentic-ml` was explicitly accepted in the US-31 plan; the older pending-name statement is superseded by that recorded decision. Build backend, initial version, and development-tool choices are implementation-plan decisions. Configuration schemas, broader API compatibility/versioning, initialization behavior, and remaining experiment commands do not block Milestone 0 and must be resolved before their dependent capabilities are implemented. Pending ADR-002–006 mechanisms do not block the minimal Milestone 0 package foundation.

### Pending decisions

- **ADR-002:** Expose harness through Python API and CLI initially for developer and interactive coding-assistant use without an adapter. Managed delegation uses verified adapters; consider an MCP server later. Exact commands and managed product/interface choices remain pending.
- **ADR-003:** Start with a lightweight durable state-machine orchestrator; evaluate agent orchestration frameworks if complexity requires.
- **ADR-004:** Hybrid ML operations: standardized capabilities plus sandboxed custom Python code, with project-local registration of user-supplied algorithms and feature preparation through versioned public interfaces. Components may come from project code or pinned dependencies; using them requires no harness modifications. Supplied code is immutable by default, with explicit developer approval required to change immutable components. This proposed decision remains pending.
- **ADR-005:** Choose configurable project-associated DVC storage, MLflow backend/artifact storage, and durable workflow-state configuration, including single-machine local defaults; DVC data versioning/pipelines and MLflow experiment tracking are selected stack components.
- **ADR-006:** Define the authorization and isolation model for data connectors, generated code, and interactive notebook kernels, including protected-test isolation, project/harness filesystem boundaries, assistant-process/tool/workspace access in interactive and managed modes, protected evaluator resources and approval channels. For the current toolkit experiment version, use unauthenticated scoped approval records under US-03-SC-01 below; authenticated approval is deferred. Development/testing gates are unchanged. Other mechanisms remain pending; it must enforce each milestone’s required access and authorization controls before the governed capability is delivered. Milestone 1 requires execution/extraction boundaries; Milestone 2 requires protected-test isolation for predictive feature comparison; Milestone 3 adds authorized independent final evaluation; Milestone 4 extends boundaries to managed agent and interactive work.
- **ADR-007 remaining details:** Verify additional Python versions to verify beyond the required Python 3.12 baseline, API compatibility/versioning, configuration schemas, and remaining CLI/API commands; GitHub installation, full commit pinning, and the agentic-ml CLI/init sequence are selected above.


### US-02 IP1 — Initialization-specific decision proposals

**Status: Initialization slice accepted at the US-02 IP1 gate, 2026-10-30 (“i approve ip1; commit changes and I authorize ip2”).** These bounded refinements do not accept ADR-002/005/006/007 in full. The [IP1 contract report](../../verification/us-02-ip1.md) supplies concrete interfaces, shapes, alternatives resolved and verification boundaries.

- **ADR-002/007 interface slice:** Keep `agentic-ml init` and expose a typed `agentic_ml.initialization` API with explicit project root, conflict diagnostics and stage results. Use schema version 0.1 for draft initialization configuration. Prefer explicit unconfigured choices over guessed experiment decisions. Preserve existing project files and the full-SHA harness source; use lossless additive TOML edits and a setup journal because external tools cannot participate in one filesystem transaction.
- **ADR-005 storage slice:** Local DVC metadata/cache and a configured local filesystem remote; explicit SQLite MLflow backend and filesystem artifact root; initial durable JSON state that grants no approval. Support explicit external local paths. This avoids service provisioning while retaining project-associated configuration. Remote deployments and complete workflow recovery remain pending.
- **ADR-006 setup slice:** Setup flags authorize only validated project/store writes. No implicit raw-data reads, kernel starts, agent authentication, experiment runs or approval grants. Reject symlink/overlap/conflict destinations and credential-bearing URI settings. A setup journal/lock is not execution isolation or an approval service; those enforcement mechanisms remain pending before their governed capabilities ship.
- **Milestone dependency slice:** Initialize CPU tabular/scikit-learn and notebook/storage dependencies; later framework stories supply LightGBM/PyTorch integrations. Retain nbclient/ipykernel; editor tooling is installed separately. Joint resolution and installed behavior must be verified in subsequent phases, not inferred from this design record.

**Consequences:** IP2–IP4 implement only after the IP1 gate approves the linked contracts and refined public test boundaries. Invalidated contracts require scope review. No current executable capability or broader accepted decision changes here.

### US-03 IP1 — Input-resolution and delegated-approval proposals

**Status: Bounded IP1 contracts approved by developer “i approve the changes” (2026-10-31).
Unauthenticated experiment approval scope approved by US-03-SC-01.** These bounded
decisions do not accept ADR-002/006/007 in full. The
[US-03 contract report](../../verification/us-03-ip1.md) specifies exact fields,
public interfaces, precedence, preservation and verification boundaries.

- **ADR-002/007 input slice:** Add `plan resolve/inspect/verify`, typed
  `agentic_ml.planning` interfaces and strict version 1.0 Markdown/YAML/schema
  contracts. Resolve structured decisions without natural-language inference.
  Keep initialization 0.1 drafts unchanged; users supply reviewed 1.0 inputs at
  separate paths. Store exact sources and a deterministic SHA-256 plan identity
  in immutable local bundles. Readiness is recomputed and grants no execution
  permission; registry/default/candidate validation remains US-05.
- **ADR-006 experiment approval slice — scope approved 2026-10-31:** Replace the
  initial SSH-signature/protected-policy/distinct-OS-identity proposal with
  project-local unauthenticated approval/revocation records. Preserve exact
  project/experiment/plan/decision binding and current revocation/staleness
  checks; record `authentication: none` and self-declared reviewer. No keys,
  protected system directory or special host. An agent or other workspace writer
  can fabricate records or alter history; authorship and tamper resistance are
  not established by checksums or record validation. Authenticated approval is
  deferred future hardening; future US-23-AC-02 remains undelivered.
- **Verification:** IP4 must test matching/missing/malformed/stale/revoked and
  wrong-scope records through installed CLI/API on both wheel paths. Removed
  signature and separate-principal tests are deferred assurance, not passing
  evidence. Full-suite/distribution and other applicable checks remain required.
- **Development/testing boundary:** The developer clarified that unauthenticated
  approval applies only when a data scientist uses the toolkit in an experiment.
  All existing harness development/testing approval gates, test-boundary review,
  verification, story acceptance and publication requirements remain unchanged.
  General execution/kernel and protected-test isolation stay with their owning
  capabilities; experiment approval records cannot approve harness changes.

**Decision references:** Developer “Authenticated approval is a bit much for this
version of the toolkit. For now let's use unauthenticated approval in
experiments.” and “The change in authentication is only for when a data scientist
is using the toolkit in an experiment. I still want the existing approval gates
currently in place for development and testing.” See
[US-03-SC-01](../../plans/milestone-1-us-03.md#us-03-sc-01--unauthenticated-experiment-approvals-2026-10-31).

**Consequences:** Revised concrete contract and public test boundaries approved.
IP2 execution awaits explicit authorization. No executable behavior or future authenticated capability is delivered here.
# Agentic ML Development Harness — Design

**Version:** 0.13
**Status:** Proposed specification; ADR-001 accepted; ADR-007 installation decisions accepted
**Date:** 2026-10-28

## Reading map and document authority

Start with this overview for scope, architecture, and workflow phases. Before implementing a capability, read its topic documents below and follow their related-contract links for affected behavior. Read the applicable milestone, acceptance-criteria mapping, and accepted or pending architecture decisions as well.

GitHub issues govern implementation scope and recorded scope decisions. [User stories](user-stories.md) define product requirements and stable acceptance-criterion IDs. This design and its topic documents provide supporting contracts; examples remain proposed unless explicitly settled. Resolve conflicts before implementing affected behavior.

| Task or question | Required topic documents |
|---|---|
| Installation, initialization, configuration, public interfaces, custom components, runtime guidance | [Interfaces and configuration](design/interfaces-and-configuration.md); [execution and governance](design/execution-and-governance.md) |
| Execution, notebook isolation, evaluation, tracking, restoration, cancellation, recovery, approvals, agent integration | [Execution and governance](design/execution-and-governance.md); [interfaces and configuration](design/interfaces-and-configuration.md) |
| Extraction, acquisition, splits, feature engineering | [Data and features](design/data-and-features.md); [interfaces and configuration](design/interfaces-and-configuration.md); [execution and governance](design/execution-and-governance.md) |
| Acceptance coverage and verification datasets | [Acceptance traceability](design/acceptance-traceability.md), then the linked contracts for the affected criteria |
| Delivery scope, prerequisites, sequencing | [Milestone delivery](design/milestone-delivery.md) |
| Package, resource, and experiment-project locations | [Repository layout](design/repository-layout.md); [interfaces and configuration](design/interfaces-and-configuration.md) |
| Accepted choices and unresolved mechanisms | [Architecture decisions](design/architecture-decisions.md) |

Each detailed section has one authoritative location. Section numbers are retained for continuity with earlier reviews; historical line numbers refer to the versions reviewed. Topic documents share the design version and status above. Reorganization does not approve pending decisions or change delivery scope.

## 1. Executive Summary

Build an agent-independent machine learning development harness for tabular ML and deep learning. Coding assistants can invoke the harness interactively through its public CLI/API, while a workflow orchestrator within the installed package can delegate tasks through managed agent adapters; distinct execution and evaluation components independently execute, validate, and track experiments. Development is supervised: agents may iterate within approved workflow phases and budgets, while developers approve workflow phase transitions and expanded data-access scope.

The harness is a versioned Python dependency installed into a separate user experiment repository. That repository is the unit users own, review, version, and share: it contains experiment briefs, configuration, agent-generated notebooks and Python code, and data-versioning metadata. Notebooks are the primary user interface for inspecting, running, and refining experiments; the harness provides reusable capabilities and independent execution and evaluation controls.

A central design principle is **hierarchical closed-loop ML development**:

## Planning terminology

- **Milestone:** A group of user stories. A target date is optional. Milestones 0–6 define cumulative, usable product increments in delivery order. Milestone 50 collects ongoing technical environment improvements as they are identified, outside the product delivery sequence. Milestone 99 groups deferred enhancements without committing their order.
- **Implementation phase:** A group of granular tasks within a user story's implementation plan, ending with an explicit developer approval gate.
- **Workflow phase:** A stage of an ML experiment run through the harness, such as feature engineering or final evaluation.
- **Approval gate:** A developer decision permitting progression after reviewing the required evidence.

Implementation plans follow **milestone → user story → implementation phase → tasks**. Identify each implementation phase by story and local phase number, for example, **US-11 / Implementation Phase 2: Build extraction**. For stories delivered across milestones, also identify the milestone and acceptance criteria covered by the plan.

Each implementation phase specifies its tasks, required review evidence, and approval criteria. Complete the tasks and present the evidence, then pause until the developer explicitly approves progression. Requested changes remain within the current implementation phase. These development approvals are separate from the workflow phase approvals enforced by the harness during an experiment. Always qualify “phase” as “implementation phase” or “workflow phase” in prose.

## Proposed direction

- Support tabular ML and deep learning, initially with scikit-learn, LightGBM, and PyTorch.
- Provide reusable orchestration, agent integration, approval handling, execution, and independent evaluation in an installable Python package.
- Keep notebooks, experiment configuration, custom algorithms, and preprocessing in separate user experiment repositories.
- Use MLflow for experiment tracking and DVC for data versioning and reproducible pipelines.
- Support model-improvement and data-improvement loops within approved scope and budgets.

The installation commands and repository layouts in the design document describe the intended implementation; they are not yet a runnable setup guide.

Build and check distributable packages using the [distribution verification commands](docs/development/distribution.md#distribution-builds-and-installed-verification). Both wheel paths pass locally on macOS and in hosted Linux/Python 3.12 CI, including verified build/resource failure diagnostics; see [US-33 evidence](docs/verification/us-33-ip3.md). US-33 is complete and developer-accepted.
# Retained development evidence

## Retained development records

Use the harness repository's `.dev-records/` directory for raw development evidence that must survive disposable environment and workspace cleanup. Git ignores this directory. Keep concise, reviewed verification reports in the tracked `docs/verification/` directory and reference the corresponding record locations from those reports.

Verification records use the following layout. Each invocation has a unique directory; concurrent runs must not overwrite one another's records.

```text
.dev-records/
  verification/
    <timestamp>-<commit>-<unique-run-id>/
      summary.json
      commands.json
      identities/
      logs/
```

The records identify the story and acceptance criteria when applicable, source commit and relevant working-tree changes, operating system and tool versions, commands and working directories, stdout/stderr, artifact checksums, installed package and environment identities, and outcomes including failed or incomplete checks. Record unavailable information explicitly. Exclude credentials and sensitive dataset contents from retained records.

Retain these records for the lifetime of agentic-ml development. Automated environment, cache, pytest, and workspace cleanup must preserve `.dev-records/`. Large virtual environments, installer caches, and datasets belong in disposable workspaces rather than this directory. Verification commands must report the absolute record location so that contributors can find the evidence after cleanup.

Contributors are responsible for backing up `.dev-records/` and preserving or transferring it before deleting or replacing a checkout. Ignoring the directory does not protect it from `git clean -fdx`, which can delete ignored files; preserve these records before any such operation. Records from separate checkouts must be included in the backup. Existing historical evidence must not be deleted or migrated automatically.

The four standalone verification drivers implement this layout. Their `RECORDS`
lines identify each invocation; composed initialization/planning commands report
parent and child records. Parent summaries link child records, and child summaries
identify the parent. Logs and manifests survive default successful removal of
owned environments/private caches. Child retention allows all parent probes to
finish; the parent's summary owns the final cleanup result. Source fixtures and
project files are preserved separately from environments.

`summary.json` separates `verification_exit_code` from `cleanup` (`not attempted`,
`pending`, `complete`, `retained` or `failed`). A null exit code denotes incomplete
verification. `commands.json` lists attempted stages and log paths, including
failed/spawn-failed commands. `identities/` contains selected manifests and their
checksums; unavailable identities must not be interpreted as passing probes.
Record-write failure prevents cleanup. Verification failure and `--keep-workspace`
retain environments; cleanup failure reports a nonzero command result while
preserving the verification outcome. See [driver usage](distribution.md).

No historical records are moved or deleted. Forced termination may prevent final
status writes or child output capture; incomplete records and workspaces need
inspection. Earlier drivers stored evidence only in temporary workspaces; copy
historical evidence needed for lifetime retention into this layout manually,
preserving its original location and source identity. Pytest-owned workspaces
under US-36 keep durable records outside pytest retention paths. Successful
test/shared trees can disappear before session exit, including source/project
files that standalone drivers normally preserve. Driver `RECORDS` locations,
linked manifests and logs remain in the checkout's durable records directory.
Fixture projects that intentionally model records for a regression test are
temporary test data; they do not replace retained development evidence.

Pytest `--keep-test-workspaces` preserves successful test trees for inspection;
driver `--keep-workspace` alone only preserves them for remaining test consumers.
Explicitly retained and interrupted trees need deliberate review and cleanup.
Do not migrate or remove historical evidence as part of that cleanup. Consult
[pytest retention](verification.md#pytest-workspace-ownership-and-retention) for
shared-fixture lifetimes, one-invocation failure retention and isolated bases.

## 1. Executive Summary

Build an agent-independent machine learning development harness for tabular ML and deep learning. Coding assistants can invoke the harness interactively through its public CLI/API, while a workflow orchestrator within the installed package can delegate tasks through managed agent adapters; distinct execution and evaluation components independently execute, validate, and track experiments. Development is supervised: agents may iterate within approved workflow phases and budgets, while developers approve workflow phase transitions and expanded data-access scope.

The harness is a versioned Python dependency installed into a separate user experiment repository. That repository is the unit users own, review, version, and share: it contains experiment briefs, configuration, agent-generated notebooks and Python code, and data-versioning metadata. Notebooks are the primary user interface for inspecting, running, and refining experiments; the harness provides reusable capabilities and independent execution and evaluation controls.

A central design principle is **hierarchical closed-loop ML development**:

## Planning terminology

- **Milestone:** A group of user stories. A target date is optional. Milestones 0–6 define cumulative, usable product increments in delivery order. Milestone 50 collects ongoing technical environment improvements as they are identified, outside the product delivery sequence. Milestone 99 groups deferred enhancements without committing their order.
- **Implementation phase:** A group of granular tasks within a user story's implementation plan, ending with an explicit developer approval gate.
- **Workflow phase:** A stage of an ML experiment run through the harness, such as feature engineering or final evaluation.
- **Approval gate:** A developer decision permitting progression after reviewing the required evidence.

Implementation plans follow **milestone → user story → implementation phase → tasks**. Identify each implementation phase by story and local phase number, for example, **US-11 / Implementation Phase 2: Build extraction**. For stories delivered across milestones, also identify the milestone and acceptance criteria covered by the plan.

Each implementation phase specifies its tasks, required review evidence, and approval criteria. Complete the tasks and present the evidence, then pause until the developer explicitly approves progression. Requested changes remain within the current implementation phase. These development approvals are separate from the workflow phase approvals enforced by the harness during an experiment. Always qualify “phase” as “implementation phase” or “workflow phase” in prose.

## Proposed direction

- Support tabular ML and deep learning, initially with scikit-learn, LightGBM, and PyTorch.
- Provide reusable orchestration, agent integration, approval handling, execution, and independent evaluation in an installable Python package.
- Keep notebooks, experiment configuration, custom algorithms, and preprocessing in separate user experiment repositories.
- Use MLflow for experiment tracking and DVC for data versioning and reproducible pipelines.
- Support model-improvement and data-improvement loops within approved scope and budgets.

The installation commands and repository layouts in the design document describe the intended implementation; they are not yet a runnable setup guide.

Build and check distributable packages using the [distribution verification commands](docs/development/distribution.md#distribution-builds-and-installed-verification). Both wheel paths pass locally on macOS and in hosted Linux/Python 3.12 CI, including verified build/resource failure diagnostics; see [US-33 evidence](docs/verification/us-33-ip3.md). US-33 is complete and developer-accepted.

def plan_diagnostics(plan: dict[str, JSONValue]) -> tuple[Diagnostic, ...]:
    """Restore typed diagnostics from a freshly derived plan."""
    result = []
    for item in sequence(plan["diagnostics"]):
        value = mapping(item)
        result.append(
            Diagnostic(
                str(value["code"]),
                str(value["field"]),
                str(value["source_path"]),
                cast(int | None, value["line"]),
                cast(int | None, value["column"]),
                str(value["message"]),
            )
        )
    return tuple(result)


def verify_evidence(
    access: ProjectAccess, plan_id: str, check_current: bool, *, approvals: bool = True
) -> tuple[VerificationResult, dict[str, JSONValue] | None]:
    """Recompute the preserved plan and its current-source requirements."""
    from agentic_ml.planning.storage import read_bundle

    plan, sources = read_bundle(access, plan_id)
    validate(plan, "plan", "plan.json", {})
    config_input = next(
        mapping(item)
        for item in sequence(plan["inputs"])
        if mapping(item)["name"] == "experiment.yaml"
    )
    if mapping(plan["project"])["root"] != str(access.root):
        fail("stale_source", "project.root", "plan.json")
    derived = prepare(access, str(config_input["path"]), dict(sources), preserved=True)
    if canonical(derived) != canonical(plan):
        fail("corrupt_plan", "derived_decisions", "plan.json")
    if check_current:
        for item in sequence(plan["inputs"]):
            entry = mapping(item)
            try:
                current = access.read(str(entry["path"]))
            except (OSError, InputError):
                fail("stale_source", str(entry["name"]), str(entry["path"]))
            if current != sources[str(entry["name"])]:
                fail("stale_source", str(entry["name"]), str(entry["path"]))
    access.recheck()
    diagnostics = plan_diagnostics(plan)
    ids: tuple[str, ...] = ()
    if (
        approvals
        and diagnostics
        and all(d.code == "approval_required" for d in diagnostics)
    ):
        from agentic_ml.approvals.models import ApprovalError
        from agentic_ml.approvals.verification import approval_ids

        try:
            ids = approval_ids(access, plan_id, plan)
            if ids:
                diagnostics = ()
        except (ApprovalError, ValueError, TypeError, KeyError) as error:
            if isinstance(error, ApprovalError) and error.operational:
                raise PlanningError(error.code, str(error)) from error
            diagnostics = (
                Diagnostic(
                    "invalid_approval",
                    "approvals",
                    ".agentic-ml/plan-approvals",
                    1,
                    1,
                    "Approval evidence is invalid.",
                ),
            )
    return VerificationResult(
        plan_id,
        "blocked" if diagnostics else "input_ready",
        diagnostics,
        True,
        "none",
        ids,
    ), plan


def checked_evidence(
    project_root: Path, plan_id: str, check_current: bool
) -> tuple[VerificationResult, dict[str, JSONValue] | None]:
    """Convert invalid evidence into safe public verification diagnostics."""
    access: ProjectAccess | None = None
    try:
        access = ProjectAccess(project_root)
        return verify_evidence(access, plan_id, check_current)
    except InputError as error:
        return VerificationResult(plan_id, "blocked", (error.diagnostic,), False), None
    except (
        ValueError,
        KeyError,
        StopIteration,
        TypeError,
        FileNotFoundError,
        NotADirectoryError,
    ):
        return VerificationResult(
            plan_id,
            "blocked",
            (
                Diagnostic(
                    "corrupt_plan",
                    "",
                    "plan.json",
                    None,
                    None,
                    "Plan evidence is missing, invalid or corrupt.",
                ),
            ),
            False,
        ), None
    except OSError as error:
        raise PlanningError(
            "plan_io", "Unable to read preserved planning evidence."
        ) from error
    finally:
        if access is not None:
            access.close()


def verify_plan(
    *, project_root: Path, plan_id: str, check_current: bool = False
) -> VerificationResult:
    """Recompute integrity and readiness; optionally compare current source bytes."""
    return checked_evidence(project_root, plan_id, check_current)[0]


def inspect_plan(*, project_root: Path, plan_id: str) -> PlanInspection:
    """Return verified preserved evidence without trusting a stored readiness flag."""
    result, plan = checked_evidence(project_root, plan_id, False)
    return PlanInspection(
        plan_id,
        result.status,
        result.integrity,
        plan,
        result.diagnostics,
        result.authentication,
        result.approval_ids,
    )

# Distribution verification

## Distribution builds and installed verification

From the repository root, build into a fresh output directory and verify both paths:

```sh
uv build --out-dir dist
uv run --locked python tests/packaging/verify_distributions.py --artifacts-dir dist
uv run --locked python tests/installation/verify_initialization.py --artifacts-dir dist
```

Use an empty output directory for each reviewed build. If `dist` already contains artifacts from an earlier version, use a new directory in both commands. The driver requires exactly one wheel and one `.tar.gz` source distribution and rejects missing or ambiguous candidates. These same commands are configured in hosted CI. Both hosted wheel paths and separate build/resource failure-and-correction cases passed verification; see the [IP3 report](../verification/us-33-ip3.md).

The driver creates a unique temporary workspace outside the checkout and prints its path. For each wheel it creates an unseeded Python 3.12 environment with `uv venv --no-project --python 3.12`, installs the wheel normally with `uv pip install --python ENV/bin/python WHEEL`, and probes it from a separate minimal experiment project. The probe uses isolated Python (`-I`) and an absolute installed `agentic-ml --version` entrypoint. It verifies CLI exit/stdout/stderr, wheel and installed version agreement, public imports, import/metadata paths, absence of editable installation and contributor dependencies, and independently specified resource contents. Both standalone probes retain an independently specified list of the harness's direct runtime requirements. They derive the transitive runtime inventory from installed `Requires-Dist` metadata, evaluating Python/platform markers, requested extras and version constraints. Missing or incompatible requirements, unrelated installed packages, contributor tools and type stubs fail with separate diagnostics. Distribution names use standard normalization for dots, underscores and hyphens. The pinned-project probe also checks universal-lock dependency reachability and installed version agreement; other-platform branches may remain locked without being installed. Fresh installations resolve declared dependency ranges independently of the contributor lockfile. The shared contributor helper uses `packaging`, supplied by the installed runtime dependencies, and is copied alongside the external Git-installation probe; it is not a packaged harness module. Only observed platforms count as verified. Changes to the harness's direct runtime requirements still require reviewing the independent declarations in both probes.

The second path validates source archive members, rejects links and traversal, and extracts with Python's `data` filter. It runs `uv build EXTRACTED_SOURCE --wheel --out-dir REBUILT_DIRECTORY` with build isolation, then installs that new wheel into another fresh environment. It never substitutes the direct wheel for the rebuilt wheel. Build dependencies remain separate from both runtime environments. Python path/home and active environment overrides are removed from child commands.

The initialization driver first runs those unchanged normal-wheel checks, then uses the validated source distribution to create a temporary full-SHA Git fixture. It compares every package file in both wheels with that source and each installed pinned Git package. Separate fresh CLI and existing-package API projects exercise complete initialization and reruns, including real stores, inert notebooks, imports, lock/pin preservation, Git exclusions and absent authorization. Wheel installs retain wheel origin; pinned-project installs retain Git origin. No origin metadata is fabricated, and unpublished fixture commits are local evidence. Successful commands remove only owned environments and private caches after the last probe; source fixtures and project files remain. The M1 complete-initialization test exercises the complete initialization contract; no additional CI service or editor is required.

Installed resources are read with `importlib.resources.files("agentic_ml")`:

| `templates/provisional.txt` | `Provisional Milestone 0 template; experiment initialization is unavailable.` |
| `runtime_guidance/provisional.md` | `Provisional Milestone 0 runtime guidance; experiment execution is unavailable.` |

These provisional files remain packaging sentinels. US-02 IP2 adds separate `templates/initialization/` resources and versioned draft schemas; the installed probe verifies their inventory, schema properties and inert notebook content. Environment synchronization is implemented in IP3 and local storage initialization in IP4; runtime guidance selection/loading remains subsequent work. Development `AGENTS.md` files are not installed runtime resources.

numbered invocation; shared paths wait for their last consumer. Standalone
commands retain their existing source/project preservation behavior. See
[pytest workspace ownership and retention](verification.md#pytest-workspace-ownership-and-retention)
for overrides, explicit bases, concurrent/nested runs and interruption limits.

Initialization and planning invoke distribution verification with an explicit
new child workspace and `--keep-workspace`. Child records link to parent records;
the parent reports both locations. The parent owns cleanup of the known child
environments/cache after its last consumer; it preserves extracted source,
rebuilt wheels, Git fixtures, project files and records. The child summary records
its retained outcome; the parent summary records eventual cleanup. No arbitrary
external path is adopted for deletion. Shared installer caches remain untouched.

A failed build/install/probe exits nonzero and identifies its stage and records.
A later failure cannot count as passing because the direct wheel passed. Failure
to persist records prevents cleanup. Cleanup failure exits nonzero while retaining
the original verification outcome; an already nonzero verification status takes
precedence. Diagnostics identify remaining workspace and records. No historical
workspace or evidence is deleted or migrated. Interruption may leave partial
workspaces and incomplete records; forced process termination cannot guarantee
finalization or capture of a running child's buffered output. Raw records remain
outside Git and require contributor backup.

The complete `uv run --locked pytest -n 4 --dist=loadgroup -m ""` suite builds a small real artifact fixture and checks success plus malformed wheels (missing template, altered guidance, wrong CLI version), missing/ambiguous artifacts and corrupted source archives. Source-checkout CLI regressions remain separate. Verification currently uses POSIX `bin/python` and `bin/agentic-ml` paths; Windows remains unverified. See [US-33 IP2 evidence](../verification/us-33-ip2.md) for actual local results; hosted Linux/Python 3.12 package results and failure diagnostics passed in the [IP3 report](../verification/us-33-ip3.md). A default-branch package run remains post-merge follow-up.

Reorganization does not approve pending decisions or change delivery scope. ## 1. Executive Summary Build an agent-independent machine learning development harness for tabular ML and deep learning. Coding assistants can invoke the harness interactively through its public CLI/API, while a workflow orchestrator within the installed package can delegate tasks through managed agent adapters; distinct execution and evaluation components independently execute, validate, and track experiments. Development is supervised: agents may iterate within approved workflow phases and budgets, while developers approve workflow phase transitions and expanded data-access scope. The harness is a versioned Python dependency installed into a separate user experiment repository. That repository is the unit users own, review, version, and share: it contains experiment briefs, configuration, agent-generated notebooks and Python code, and data-versioning metadata. Notebooks are the primary user interface for inspecting, running, and refining experiments; the harness provides reusable capabilities and independent execution and evaluation controls. A central design principle is **hierarchical closed-loop ML development**: - **Inner loop — model improvement:** feature engineering, training, hyperparameter optimization, and evaluation. - **Outer loop — data improvement:** data gap diagnosis, iterative acquisition, extraction, validation, dataset versioning, and retraining. ## 2. Scope and Design Decisions | Dimension | Decision | |---|---| | Orchestration | Distinct orchestration and execution/evaluation components within the installed harness package | | Agent integrations | Interactive coding-assistant use through the public CLI/API as the basic path; standardized managed adapters for harness-invoked coding assistants and specialized agents | | ML frameworks | Initial scikit-learn, LightGBM, and PyTorch; extensible | | Package management | Use `uv` for Python dependency management, lockfiles, and virtual environments | | Initial distribution | Install the Python package directly from its GitHub repository using `uv`, pinned to a full Git commit SHA; package-registry distribution is future work | | CLI and Python imports | Use `agentic-ml` as the installed CLI name and retain `agentic_ml` as the Python import/package directory name | | Repository boundary | Separate harness product repository and user experiment repositories; consume the harness as a versioned Python dependency through its public API and CLI | | Jupyter notebooks | Agent-generated notebooks in the user experiment repository are the primary experiment interface; support interactive use and automatic harness-managed execution | | Model types | Tabular classification/regression and deep learning | | Autonomy | Supervised with developer approvals at workflow phase boundaries | | Data | Extraction, EDA, feature engineering, and iterative acquisition are first-class | | Execution | Local subprocesses for the proof of concept; Ray planned for later distributed and parallel execution; container/GPU backends incrementally | | Experiment tracking | MLflow for runs, parameters, metrics, model artifacts, and experiment comparisons | | Data versioning and pipelines | DVC for dataset and derived-data versioning, dependency tracking, and reproducible pipelines; Git versions DVC metadata and pipeline definitions | | Agent instructions | Targeted `AGENTS.md` files in separate development and runtime guidance trees; runtime loading is explicit and versioned | | Experiment guidance | Developer-authored Markdown brief plus versioned YAML algorithm and hyperparameter boundaries | | Search autonomy | Agent searches only within declared boundaries; expansions are recommendations for subsequent experiments | | Deployment | Outside initial scope | ### Principles 1. Agent and ML-framework independence through versioned interfaces. 2. Explicit separation of planning/delegation, execution, evaluation, and approval. 3. Independent, evidence-based validation; agent claims alone never establish success. 4. Reproducibility, provenance, and data-to-model lineage by design. 5. Budgeted, interruptible, resumable closed loops. 6. Controlled data access and protected evaluation datasets. 7. Extensible operations: standardized tasks plus sandboxed custom code. ## 3. Development evidence or final review results .-> O X <-->|Versioned data and pipeline outputs| D[(DVC Storage)] X -->|Runs, snapshots, and model artifacts| M[(MLflow Tracking and Artifacts)] E -->|Evaluation results| M D -. Dataset and pipeline references .-> M ``` The installed harness package supplies orchestration, agent integration, approval handling, execution, and evaluation. Separation of orchestration from execution/evaluation means distinct component responsibilities within the package, rather than separate installations or repositories. Agent adapters connect to coding assistants or external agent services; those external systems need not run inside the package. Package boundaries show implementation ownership, not process or deployment boundaries. These capabilities operate in the selected experiment project's environment using its configuration and project-associated state/storage. The orchestrator coordinates approved work; execution independently enforces boundaries, and evaluation assesses results. Project-owned models and preprocessors run through harness interfaces alongside built-in components. Interactive notebook use follows the same access rules and cannot establish acceptance by itself. Protected holdout access is reserved for independent final evaluation; its feedback cannot drive development iterations. Harness manifests link DVC and MLflow records to project snapshots, component identities, approvals, and durable project-associated workflow state. ### Component responsibilities | Component | Responsibilities | |---|---| | Workflow orchestrator | Plans workflow phases, delegates tasks, maintains durable state, controls iterations, enforces approvals and budgets, resumes work | | Agent integration | Capability discovery, structured task/result exchange, cancellation, CLI/SDK/tool adapters | | Data extraction engine | Source discovery, approved queries, ingestion, snapshots, schema checks, lineage | | Data acquisition planner | Diagnose gaps, propose additional samples/labels/sources, estimate costs and expected benefit | | Data acquisition executor | Enforce recorded acquisition authorization, execute acquisition, validate and version results | | EDA/validation | Profiling, missingness, class balance, anomalies, leakage diagnostics, split strategy | | Feature engineering | Propose/fit/transform/select features, version pipelines, evaluate feature sets | | Experiment runner | Backend-independent submission, status, cancellation, resources, logs, artifacts, and checkpoints; local execution initially, Ray-backed execution later | | Framework adapters | Standardized and custom training entrypoints for scikit-learn, LightGBM, PyTorch | | Evaluation engine | Metrics, baseline comparisons, scientific validity, robustness, reproducibility | | Tracking and artifact store | MLflow records runs, parameters, metrics, and model artifacts; links to DVC dataset/pipeline versions and harness manifests for complete lineage | | Data versioning and pipelines | DVC tracks source and derived datasets, dependencies, stage outputs, and reproducible pipeline definitions; integrates with harness execution | | Approval service | Workflow phase and acquisition approvals, authorization scope, audit records | ### Harness and experiment project boundary The harness repository contains reusable execution, evaluation, tracking, agent integration, orchestration, approval handling, templates, and default runtime guidance. Each user experiment repository contains objectives, notebooks, supplied and generated code, configuration, and versioning metadata. One experiment repository may contain multiple related experiments sharing project code and dependencies. ```mermaid flowchart LR subgraph H["Harness repository"] direction TB HC["Reusable Python package
src/agentic_ml/
Orchestration, Adapters, Approvals, Execution, and Evaluation"] HR["Templates and runtime guidance
templates/ · runtime_guidance/"] HD["Package metadata and tests
pyproject.toml · tests/"] end subgraph U["User experiment repository"] direction TB UC["Project configuration

The installation arrow represents a pinned GitHub package dependency installed into the user project's Python environment. Experiment agents operate within the experiment repository and use the installed harness through its public Python API and CLI. Routine experiment work does not modify the harness installation or source repository and must not require a neighboring harness checkout. Changes to shared harness capabilities follow a separate software-development review process. ### Interactive and managed agent use - **Interactive mode:** The developer works with an external coding assistant, such as Codex, GitHub Copilot, or Claude Code, which prepares project files and invokes the harness CLI/API. No agent adapter is required, and the harness does not own the assistant session. - **Managed mode:** The orchestrator delegates bounded tasks through a configured agent adapter, receives structured results, and coordinates evaluation and further revisions. Managed support requires verification of a concrete product, interface, and version; a product name alone does not establish adapter capabilities. Both modes use the same harness-owned experiment state, plan validation, approvals, managed execution, budgets, artifact records, and independent evaluation. The assistant proposes changes and requests work; only recorded harness evidence and authorized developer decisions establish acceptance or workflow phase progression. The architecture diagram shows both directions: managed delegation through the agent integration layer and interactive CLI/API requests from an external assistant. The orchestrator operates on an explicitly selected experiment project and environment. Durable workflow state and run artifacts are stored in configured locations associated with that project, independently of the harness source tree. ## 4. Hierarchical Closed-Loop Workflow ```mermaid flowchart TD A[Define Objectives, Components, and Boundaries] --> B[Developer Approves Plan] B --> C["Execute Authorized Workflow Phase (see Workflow Phase Descriptions Below)"] C --> D[Independently Validate Workflow Phase Evidence] D --> E[Developer Reviews Workflow Phase] E -->|Advance| F[Next Workflow Phase] F --> C E -->|Revise| G[Revise Within Approved Scope] G --> C E -->|Approve Final Model| H[Complete] E -->|Reject or Stop| I[Preserve Results and Stop] ``` The diagram summarizes the workflow phase cycle. The individual workflow phases are: 1. **Problem definition:** Define the objective, target, metrics, data sources, allowed algorithms, supplied components, constraints, and budgets. Approve the task contract and plan. 2. **Data extraction and EDA:** Obtain and version data, inspect its quality and distributions, and establish training/validation/test splits. Approve the dataset assessment and split protocol. 3. **Feature engineering:** Use supplied preprocessing or develop transformations and feature sets. Fit stateful preprocessing only on training data. Compare predictive performance against an approved baseline feature set with a fixed approved reference estimator and validation protocol. This limited training/evaluation is authorized within feature engineering; broader baseline modeling follows in the next workflow phase. Review the validated pipeline, comparison evidence, and lineage. 4. **Baseline modeling:** Train simple, reproducible reference models. Approve baseline results for later comparisons. 5. **Model development:** Train and compare candidate models, including user-supplied algorithms, and improve them within approved boundaries. Review candidate evidence. 6. **Optimization:** Tune hyperparameters within the declared search space and budgets. Approve the optimization summary and candidate for final evaluation. 7. **Final evaluation:** Evaluate the selected model on the protected holdout, check robustness and reproducibility, and produce the final report. Approve or reject the model. **Each workflow phase transition requires approval.** Agents can iterate within an approved workflow phase. Valid existing artifacts can support skipping a workflow phase when that is approved in the plan. [Section 5](agentic-ml-harness-design.md#5-standard-workflow-phases-and-gates) defines the gate evidence for each workflow phase. Data acquisition is an activity that can trigger a return to earlier workflow phases, rather than an eighth workflow phase. Supplied components and authorized data acquisition fit within “Execute Authorized Workflow Phase”; their detailed requirements appear in Sections 6–8. The following rules apply: - **Workflow phases:** Initial plan approval completes problem definition. Execution then follows the configured workflow phases in [Section 5](agentic-ml-harness-design.md#5-standard-workflow-phases-and-gates): data extraction and EDA → feature engineering → baseline modeling → model development → optimization → final evaluation. Each workflow phase approval authorizes entry to the next workflow phase and its recorded scope. - **Iteration:** Agents may iterate within the current approved workflow phase, component permissions, parameter boundaries, access scope, and budgets without approval for every run. Evidence is independently validated against requirements specific to the workflow phase before developer review; only sufficient evidence permits advancement. - **Scope changes:** Workflow phase returns, expanded permissions, and changes to immutable components require authorization before execution. # Test-Driven Development

TDD is the red → green loop. This skill is the reference that makes that loop produce tests worth keeping: what a good test is, where tests go, the anti-patterns, and the rules of the loop. Every section applies on every cycle: consult them before and during the loop, not after.

When exploring the codebase, read `GLOSSARY.md` (if it exists) so test names and interface vocabulary match the project's domain language, and respect ADRs in the area you're touching.

## What a good test is

Tests verify behavior through public interfaces, not implementation details. Code can change entirely; tests shouldn't. A good test reads like a specification: "user can checkout with valid cart" tells you exactly what capability exists, and it survives refactors because it doesn't care about internal structure.

See [tests.md](tests.md) for examples and [mocking.md](mocking.md) for mocking guidelines.

## Seams: where tests go

A **seam** is the public boundary you test at: the interface where you observe behavior without reaching inside. Tests live at seams, never against internals.

**Test only at pre-agreed seams.** Before writing any test, write down the seams under test and confirm them with the user. No test is written at an unconfirmed seam. You can't test everything, so agreeing the seams up front is how testing effort lands on the critical paths and complex logic instead of every edge case.

Ask: "What's the public interface, and which seams should we test?" Give each proposed seam a one-line note on what it catches and what it misses.

When the shape of that interface is itself in question (how deep the module is, where the seam belongs, what the interface should expose), call the Skill tool with "codebase-design" for the vocabulary. It is the shared source of the module, interface, depth, seam, adapter, leverage and locality terms, and it is a reference to consult, not a session to run.

## Anti-patterns

- **Implementation-coupled**: mocks internal collaborators, tests private methods, or verifies through a side channel (querying the database instead of using the interface). The tell: the test breaks when you refactor but behavior hasn't changed.
- **Tautological**: the assertion recomputes the expected value the way the code does (`expect(add(a, b)).toBe(a + b)`, a snapshot derived by hand the same way, a constant asserted equal to itself), so it passes by construction and can never disagree with the code. Expected values must come from an independent source of truth: a known-good literal, a worked example, the spec.
- **Horizontal slicing**: writing all tests first, then all implementation. Bulk tests verify _imagined_ behavior: you test the _shape_ of things rather than user-facing behavior, the tests go insensitive to real changes, and you commit to test structure before understanding the implementation. Work in **vertical slices** instead: one test → one implementation → repeat, each test a **tracer bullet** that responds to what the last cycle taught you.

## Rules of the loop

- **Red before green.** Write the failing test first, then only enough code to pass it. Don't anticipate future tests or add speculative features.
- **One slice at a time.** One seam, one test, one minimal implementation per cycle.
- **Refactoring is not part of the loop.** It belongs to the review stage (see the `code-review` skill), not the red → green implementation cycle.

## 1. Executive Summary

Build an agent-independent machine learning development harness for tabular ML and deep learning. Coding assistants can invoke the harness interactively through its public CLI/API, while a workflow orchestrator within the installed package can delegate tasks through managed agent adapters; distinct execution and evaluation components independently execute, validate, and track experiments. Development is supervised: agents may iterate within approved workflow phases and budgets, while developers approve workflow phase transitions and expanded data-access scope.

The harness is a versioned Python dependency installed into a separate user experiment repository. That repository is the unit users own, review, version, and share: it contains experiment briefs, configuration, agent-generated notebooks and Python code, and data-versioning metadata. Notebooks are the primary user interface for inspecting, running, and refining experiments; the harness provides reusable capabilities and independent execution and evaluation controls.

A central design principle is **hierarchical closed-loop ML development**:

- **Inner loop — model improvement:** feature engineering, training, hyperparameter optimization, and evaluation.
- **Outer loop — data improvement:** data gap diagnosis, iterative acquisition, extraction, validation, dataset versioning, and retraining.

### Milestone 0 dependencies and delivery order

Milestone 0 covers US-31, US-32, and US-33. The dependencies below follow from their [acceptance criteria](../user-stories.md#milestone-0-establish-the-harness-development-foundation). They apply to portions of stories rather than requiring each prerequisite story to be complete. The delivery order is a recommendation, not an additional acceptance requirement.

**Prerequisites:** No earlier milestone is required. Python 3.12 or newer, `uv`, and the other documented contributor prerequisites support the initial development foundation (US-31-AC-01–02).

| Dependent work | Required capability | Acceptance criterion basis |
|---|---|---|
| US-31 source-checkout execution and fresh-environment smoke verification | US-33 minimal `agentic-ml --version` CLI | US-31-AC-03, US-31-AC-07; US-33-AC-06–07 |
| US-32 automated development checks | US-31 locked development tools, check configuration, and documented local commands | US-31-AC-02, US-31-AC-04–05, US-31-AC-08; US-32-AC-02–03 |
| US-33 local package builds and verification | Shared development environment and documented tooling established under US-31 | US-31-AC-02, US-31-AC-08; US-33-AC-01–04 |
| US-33 package verification in CI | US-32 CI infrastructure plus working US-33 build and installed-package checks | US-32-AC-01–04; US-33-AC-05 |

**Recommended delivery order:**

1. Establish the US-31 development foundation: package configuration, locked environment, coding conventions, automated check configuration, and local commands.
2. Add the US-33 minimal package foundation: `agentic_ml`, `agentic-ml --version`, and provisional template and runtime guidance resources.
3. Complete US-31 fresh-checkout macOS verification, including the version smoke check.
4. Establish US-32 CI using the shared local development commands.
5. Complete US-33 isolated verification of the directly built wheel and the wheel rebuilt from the source distribution, and run those checks in CI.

Local package verification and CI setup can proceed in parallel once their prerequisites exist. Treating these relationships as whole-story completion gates would create an apparent cycle: US-31 needs the minimal CLI from US-33, while US-33 uses the development foundation and CI from US-31 and US-32. Detailed implementation plans should stage those capabilities explicitly and retain their developer approval gates.

**Completion boundary:** All acceptance criteria for US-31, US-32, and US-33 must be verified to complete Milestone 0. No Milestone 1 capability is a prerequisite: Milestone 0 owns the minimal version CLI and provisional packaged resources; usable experiment initialization resources and experiment commands remain in later milestones (US-33-AC-03, US-33-AC-06).

2. Implement US-03 resolved, versioned experiment inputs and US-05 applicable configuration and boundary validation.

Milestone 99 contains US-34: contribution instructions, documented merge checks and review expectations, and enforced default-branch protection. These are deferred rather than Milestone 0 exit criteria. Advanced capability ideas above do not add approved stories to Milestone 99.

Milestone 1 extends the package foundation established in Milestone 0 and delivers reproducible extraction, basic validation and review, recorded Python/notebook execution, and source-data/run restoration without requiring an agent. # Agentic ML

An early-stage project exploring an agent-agnostic harness for machine learning experimentation and iterative data improvement.

The proposed harness provides reusable orchestration, experiment execution, independent evaluation, and reproducible evidence tracking. Developers can use it interactively through coding assistants or delegate work to managed agents. It supports notebook-centered workflows, user-supplied models and preprocessing, and developer approvals at workflow phase boundaries. The harness is installed as a Python dependency in separate, user-owned experiment repositories.

**This project is in its early days.** Initialization, versioned experiment planning,
search-boundary validation and scoped unauthenticated decision approvals are
implemented. Managed experiment execution and broader orchestration remain
subsequent work. Interfaces will change as development progresses.

For a separate experiment project, follow the [installation and initialization guide](docs/experiment-setup.md). Initialization supplies draft inputs, a synchronized environment and local storage. Managed experiment execution remains subsequent work.

## Contributor setup

Start with the [development guide](docs/development.md) for Python 3.12, uv, locked dependencies, coding conventions, and local checks. Development tooling, the minimal package, and `agentic-ml --version` are available. Fresh-checkout macOS verification passed; see the [evidence](docs/verification/us-31-ip2.md). """Atomic, descriptor-based publication of immutable semantic validation evidence."""

import hashlib
import os
import stat
import uuid

from agentic_ml.planning.models import JSONValue
from agentic_ml.planning.paths import ProjectAccess
from agentic_ml.planning.storage import canonical, check_store, write_file
from agentic_ml.validation.checks import digest, reject, schema
from agentic_ml.validation.models import ValidationError

STORE = ".agentic-ml/validations"


def publish(
    access: ProjectAccess,
    config: dict[str, JSONValue],
    registry: dict[str, JSONValue],
    source: bytes | None,
) -> str:
    """Publish a complete immutable bundle under a cooperating-writer lock."""
    check_store(access, access.read("project.yaml"), store=STORE)
    schema(config, "configuration", "invalid_validation")
    schema(registry, "registry", "invalid_validation")
    validation_id = digest(config)
    parent = access.directory(STORE, create=True)
    locked = False
    try:
        try:
            lock = os.open(
                "validate.lock",
                os.O_WRONLY | os.O_CREAT | os.O_EXCL | os.O_NOFOLLOW,
                0o600,
                dir_fd=parent,
            )
        except FileExistsError as error:
            raise ValidationError(
                "validation_busy",
                "Validation lock exists; operator review is required.",
            ) from error
        locked = True
        lock_info = os.fstat(lock)
        os.close(lock)
        try:
            info = os.stat(validation_id[7:], dir_fd=parent, follow_symlinks=False)
        except FileNotFoundError:
            info = None
        if info is not None:
            if not stat.S_ISDIR(info.st_mode):
                reject(
                    "invalid_validation",
                    "members",
                    "Use a regular validation bundle directory.",
                )
            stored, captured, selected_source = read_bundle(access, validation_id)
            if stored != config or captured != registry or selected_source != source:
                reject(
                    "invalid_validation",
                    "members",
                    "Preserve original evidence; conflicting bundles cannot be overwritten.",
                )
            access.recheck()
            return validation_id
        members = {
            "configuration.json": canonical(config),
            "registry.json": canonical(registry),
        }
        if source is not None:
            members["registry-source.yaml"] = source
        manifest: dict[str, JSONValue] = {
            "schema_version": "1.0",
            "validation_id": validation_id,
            "files": {
                name: hashlib.sha256(data).hexdigest() for name, data in members.items()
            },
        }
        members["manifest.json"] = canonical(manifest)
        stage_name = ".pending-" + uuid.uuid4().hex
        os.mkdir(stage_name, mode=0o700, dir_fd=parent)
        stage = os.open(
            stage_name, os.O_RDONLY | os.O_DIRECTORY | os.O_NOFOLLOW, dir_fd=parent
        )
        try:
            for name, content in members.items():
                write_file(stage, name, content)
            os.fsync(stage)
            access.recheck()
            current_parent = access.directory(STORE)

The initialization and planning drivers currently invoke distribution verification and then consume its installed environments, so cleanup must follow the complete consumer lifecycle rather than occur immediately after an intermediate probe. ## Milestone 99: Future enhancements This milestone groups enhancements that are not critical to current functionality. Inclusion records deferred scope rather than a commitment to delivery order. Unlike Milestones 0–6, this milestone is a backlog of future enhancements; stories can move into a delivery milestone when prioritized, preserving their acceptance criterion IDs. ### US-34: Establish contribution and review checks As a contributor, I want clear contribution instructions and consistent review checks so that I understand how to submit changes and when they are ready to merge.
