item.aggregated_output: ## Milestone 1: Complete one experiment M1 exits when a separate installed project completes classification and ASW-01–06, with MLflow artifacts and a native DVC pipeline. Correctly recorded experiments may show no gain over baseline. ### US-01: Install a pinned toolkit version As a developer, I want to install a pinned toolkit version into my own experiment repository so that my project has a reproducible environment. **Existing accepted slice:** preserve its original contract/evidence. Default-path and future training integration work is separate. Acceptance criteria: - **US-01-AC-01:** Documented bootstrap instructions cover installing `uv` and Git, creating the user Git/Python project, and installing the toolkit from GitHub at a full commit SHA. - **US-01-AC-02:** The toolkit is a normal installed dependency; runtime use requires no manually maintained toolkit checkout or installer cache. - **US-01-AC-03:** The project lockfile records the resolved toolkit revision and dependencies; the installed package exposes `agentic-ml`, `agentic_ml`, templates, and runtime guidance. - **US-01-AC-04:** An explicit toolkit upgrade changes the commit pin and lockfile, producing a new environment identity. Supporting design: [overview](agentic-ml-harness-design.md) and reading map; MVP alignment in design 0.15; Gate 3 approved. Scope history: [approved dispositions](../reviews/mvp-scope-criterion-dispositions.md). ### US-02: Initialize an experiment project As a developer, I want to initialize configuration, notebooks, dependencies, and local storage while preserving existing files so that I can start experimenting safely. **Existing accepted slice:** preserve its original contract/evidence. Default-path and future training integration work is separate. Acceptance criteria: - **US-02-AC-01:** `uv run agentic-ml init` adds project configuration, ignore rules, an initial experiment brief, search-space and execution configuration, notebook templates, and required project-package scaffolding. - **US-02-AC-02:** Initialization preserves existing files and the pinned toolkit dependency, reporting conflicts instead of silently overwriting files. - **US-02-AC-03:** Required ML and notebook execution dependencies are declared and synchronized with the project environment and lockfile. - **US-02-AC-04:** Project-associated DVC, MLflow, and durable-state storage are initialized with local defaults and configurable locations. - **US-02-AC-05:** Data access, agent authentication, and approval presentation remain explicit setup choices; initialization grants no execution or data-access authorization, and credentials remain outside committed configuration. US-39-AC-01 owns runnable defaults/draft-schema compatibility. Accepted initialization supplies drafts, not an implemented experiment runner. Supporting design: [overview](agentic-ml-harness-design.md) and reading map; MVP alignment in design 0.15; Gate 3 approved. Scope history: [approved dispositions](../reviews/mvp-scope-criterion-dispositions.md). ### US-03: Define experiment objectives and boundaries As a data scientist, I want to describe objectives and constraints in Markdown and declare search boundaries in YAML so that agents work toward my intended outcome. **Existing accepted slice:** preserve its original contract/evidence. Default-path and future training integration work is separate. Acceptance criteria: - **US-03-AC-01:** The experiment brief captures data, target, task type, feature guidance, metric and direction, split constraints, algorithm mode, and budgets, including explicitly delegated decisions. - **US-03-AC-02:** Search-space YAML declares allowed algorithms, fixed parameters, and tunable choices or ranges; execution configuration cannot expand these boundaries. - **US-03-AC-03:** Resolved inputs produce a versioned plan containing the effective decisions, source references, and checksums before dependent execution. - **US-03-AC-04:** Ambiguous or conflicting requirements block affected runs until resolved; delegated decisions require approval before use. - **US-03-AC-05:** Relative input paths resolve against the experiment repository root, with the notebook working directory recorded explicitly. Strict explicit APIs retain readiness rules and unauthenticated-record limitations under [US-03-SC-01](../plans/milestone-1-us-03.md#us-03-sc-01--unauthenticated-experiment-approvals-2026-10-31). US-39-AC-01/02 own the simpler basic workflow; accepted contracts are not silently changed. Supporting design: [overview](agentic-ml-harness-design.md) and reading map; MVP alignment in design 0.15; Gate 3 approved. Scope history: [approved dispositions](../reviews/mvp-scope-criterion-dispositions.md). ### US-05: Reject invalid configurations before execution As a data scientist, I want invalid algorithms, parameters, and search configurations rejected before training so that compute is spent on valid candidates. **Existing accepted slice:** preserve its original contract/evidence. Default-path and future training integration work is separate. Acceptance criteria: - **US-05-AC-01:** Validation checks registered algorithm identifiers, task compatibility, parameter names, types, defaults, and compatible combinations. - **US-05-AC-02:** Categorical choices are nonempty; numeric bounds are ordered and inclusive; integer ranges yield integers; logarithmic bounds are strictly positive. - **US-05-AC-03:** Fixed values remain fixed, and omitted parameters use recorded registry defaults without becoming tunable. - **US-05-AC-04:** Invalid inputs produce actionable validation errors before training starts. - **US-05-AC-05:** As training entrypoints are introduced, every candidate submitted through Python, custom code, or notebooks receives the same boundary checks. Accepted validation metadata does not establish training support. AC-05 future training/custom/notebook integrations remain open; supported-call validation does not constrain arbitrary external Python. Supporting design: [overview](agentic-ml-harness-design.md) and reading map; MVP alignment in design 0.15; Gate 3 approved. Scope history: [approved dispositions](../reviews/mvp-scope-criterion-dispositions.md). ### US-10: Run and inspect local experiments As a data scientist, I want to run local experiments and inspect logs, status and artifacts so that I can diagnose execution failures. Acceptance criteria: - **US-10-AC-01:** Run a local experiment and expose logs, final result status and artifact locations. - **US-10-AC-02:** Record completion or failure with available diagnostics. - **US-10-AC-03:** Limit search to configured maximum candidate trials through the supported runner/search path. - **US-10-AC-04:** Unsuccessful model performance is distinguishable from execution failure when modeling is added. - **US-10-AC-05:** Preserve available completed-trial results and failure/interruption evidence when execution can finalize. Supporting design: [overview](agentic-ml-harness-design.md) and reading map; MVP alignment in design 0.15; Gate 3 approved. Scope history: [approved dispositions](../reviews/mvp-scope-criterion-dispositions.md). ### US-11: Extract local experiment data As a data scientist, I want to prepare local CSV/Parquet files using selection, filtering and joins so that I can start with traceable data. Acceptance criteria: - **US-11-AC-01:** Read local CSV/Parquet and support configured column selection, filtering and joins; permit project-owned extraction functions. - **US-11-AC-02:** Report local source schemas and metadata needed for extraction. - **US-11-AC-03:** Execute explicitly configured local extraction operations and report their configuration. - **US-11-AC-04:** Record source paths/content identities, extraction settings and time, and output checksum/DVC reference. - **US-11-AC-05:** Extraction failures are reported without presenting incomplete output as a validated dataset. Supporting design: [overview](agentic-ml-harness-design.md) and reading map; MVP alignment in design 0.15; Gate 3 approved. Scope history: [approved dispositions](../reviews/mvp-scope-criterion-dispositions.md). ### US-12: Validate data and define reproducible splits As a data scientist, I want to check data quality and record distinct partitions so that training and evaluation use suitable inputs. Acceptance criteria: - **US-12-AC-01:** Validation checks schema, row counts, types, nulls, duplicates, and configured quality rules, reporting mismatches and failures. - **US-12-AC-05:** Report validation results and block supported pipeline steps when configured required checks fail. - **US-12-AC-02:** Provide basic distributions, missingness and classification target balance. - **US-12-AC-03:** Record seeded train/validation/test partitions; accept explicit user-supplied partitions for time/group problems and check row membership/disjointness. Supporting design: [overview](agentic-ml-harness-design.md) and reading map; MVP alignment in design 0.15; Gate 3 approved. Scope history: [approved dispositions](../reviews/mvp-scope-criterion-dispositions.md). ### US-13: Version and restore datasets with DVC As a data scientist, I want to track and restore datasets with native DVC so that experiment inputs can be identified and reproduced. Acceptance criteria: - **US-13-AC-01:** DVC versions source snapshots, split manifests, and derived datasets as those artifacts are introduced. - **US-13-AC-02:** Git tracks DVC metadata and relevant manifests while dataset content resides in the configured cache/storage and is excluded from Git. Supporting design: [overview](agentic-ml-harness-design.md) and reading map; MVP alignment in design 0.15; Gate 3 approved. Scope history: [approved dispositions](../reviews/mvp-scope-criterion-dispositions.md). ### US-14: Build and compare authored feature pipelines As a data scientist, I want to execute authored feature pipelines and compare validation results so that feature changes have measurable evidence. Acceptance criteria: - **US-14-AC-01:** Describe authored scikit-learn pipeline steps, parameters, selected columns and training-only fit scope. - **US-14-AC-02:** Execute authored transformations and record pipeline settings, dependencies, output references and source-data identity. - **US-14-AC-03:** Compare authored feature variants using the same split, estimator/settings and metric; report direction-aware gains/ties/regressions. - **US-14-AC-04:** Link feature/pipeline artifacts to source datasets and verify expected outputs through supported paths. - **US-14-AC-05:** Use explicitly authored or supplied feature candidates. Supporting design: [overview](agentic-ml-harness-design.md) and reading map; MVP alignment in design 0.15; Gate 3 approved. Scope history: [approved dispositions](../reviews/mvp-scope-criterion-dispositions.md). ### US-15: Preserve training-only preprocessing As a data scientist, I want to fit preprocessing on training rows and preserve fitted state so that validation and inference use consistent transformations. Acceptance criteria: - **US-15-AC-01:** Fit preprocessing only on training rows and reuse fitted state for validation/test/inference. - **US-15-AC-02:** Reject supported-path partition overlap and improper fit scope; test for train-only fitting with independently defined expectations. - **US-15-AC-03:** Preserve fitted pipeline, feature settings and declared schema plus committed code/dependency references. Supporting design: [overview](agentic-ml-harness-design.md) and reading map; MVP alignment in design 0.15; Gate 3 approved. Scope history: [approved dispositions](../reviews/mvp-scope-criterion-dispositions.md). ### US-18: Train scikit-learn models As a data scientist, I want to train CPU tabular classification and regression models so that I can compare baselines and candidates. Acceptance criteria: - **US-18-AC-01:** Deliver classification in M1 and regression in M2 using scikit-learn on CPU. - **US-18-AC-02:** Train and record a reproducible baseline before comparing candidates. - **US-18-AC-03:** Use native compatible estimator/pipeline fit, predict and persistence operations. - **US-18-AC-04:** Each run records effective parameters, framework/library identities, metrics, model artifacts, and feature/data lineage. AC-01 spans M1 classification and M2 regression; M1 alone does not complete it. Other ML frameworks are deferred. Supporting design: [overview](agentic-ml-harness-design.md) and reading map; MVP alignment in design 0.15; Gate 3 approved. Scope history: [approved dispositions](../reviews/mvp-scope-criterion-dispositions.md). ### US-20: Tune within declared search limits As a data scientist, I want to run validated searches with a maximum trial count so that tuning stays within declared parameter and trial boundaries. Acceptance criteria: - **US-20-AC-01:** Candidates use only declared algorithms, fixed values, categorical choices, and numeric ranges; omitted defaults cannot be tuned. - **US-20-AC-02:** Validate candidates before training through supported toolkit/script/notebook execution paths. - **US-20-AC-03:** Enforce a configured maximum trial count and preserve completed trial results. - **US-20-AC-04:** Summarize candidates, validation scores, best selection, trial count and elapsed time. Supporting design: [overview](agentic-ml-harness-design.md) and reading map; MVP alignment in design 0.15; Gate 3 approved. Scope history: [approved dispositions](../reviews/mvp-scope-criterion-dispositions.md). ### US-21: Evaluate experiment outputs consistently As a data scientist, I want to compute consistent metrics and supported split/fitting checks so that I can assess results against a baseline. Acceptance criteria: - **US-21-AC-01:** Compute/check status and expected outputs from execution evidence, rather than narrative claims. - **US-21-AC-02:** Check supported split disjointness and train-only preprocessing fitting. - **US-21-AC-03:** Compute configured metrics consistently and compare against baseline with explicit direction. - **US-21-AC-05:** Report execution failure, configured validation failure and insufficient quality distinctly. Supporting design: [overview](agentic-ml-harness-design.md) and reading map; MVP alignment in design 0.15; Gate 3 approved. Scope history: [approved dispositions](../reviews/mvp-scope-criterion-dispositions.md). ### US-24: Evaluate a selected model on a separate test partition As a data scientist, I want to run final testing after validation-based model selection so that test scores do not drive the supported tuning workflow. Acceptance criteria: - **US-24-AC-02:** Evaluate the selected fitted pipeline on a separate test partition after validation-based selection. - **US-24-AC-03:** Keep test scores out of the supported tuning/feature-selection path; document no retuning on final scores. - **US-24-AC-04:** Report unsuccessful final evaluation as a result rather than silently resume tuning. Supporting design: [overview](agentic-ml-harness-design.md) and reading map; MVP alignment in design 0.15; Gate 3 approved. Scope history: [approved dispositions](../reviews/mvp-scope-criterion-dispositions.md). ### US-26: Record and compare experiment results As a data scientist, I want to link MLflow results to code, configuration and DVC data so that I can inspect and compare recorded experiments. Acceptance criteria: - **US-26-AC-01:** Record MLflow run status, parameters, metrics, outputs and artifact locations with a stable run reference. - **US-26-AC-02:** Link MLflow results to DVC data identity, committed experiment revision and effective configuration. - **US-26-AC-03:** Provenance includes the toolkit repository URL, full commit SHA, package version, build identity where available, and project lockfile/environment identity. - **US-26-AC-04:** Record committed entrypoint/project code/configuration references and save the executed notebook when used. - **US-26-AC-05:** Check expected output presence and report failures separately from successful process exit. - **US-26-AC-06:** MLflow comparisons expose effective parameters, metrics, execution status, and model artifacts for baseline and candidate runs. - **US-26-AC-07:** Produce a concise result summary with model, configured metrics, baseline comparison and validation outcomes. - **US-26-AC-08:** Link model/pipeline artifacts to DVC data, committed code/configuration and locked environment references. - **US-26-AC-09:** Link report claims to recorded numerical evaluation results/artifacts. - **US-26-AC-12:** Allow results to locate their MLflow run and MLflow metadata to locate committed project/config/data references. Supporting design: [overview](agentic-ml-harness-design.md) and reading map; MVP alignment in design 0.15; Gate 3 approved. Scope history: [approved dispositions](../reviews/mvp-scope-criterion-dispositions.md). ### US-27: Run and reproduce native DVC pipelines As a data scientist, I want to run native DVC stages from committed experiment inputs so that I can reproduce results and reuse valid outputs. Acceptance criteria: - **US-27-AC-05:** DVC pipeline definitions record stage dependencies, parameters, and outputs, with resolved hashes preserved in `dvc.lock`. - **US-27-AC-06:** Stage working directories and paths are explicit and consistent with toolkit execution. Supporting design: [overview](agentic-ml-harness-design.md) and reading map; MVP alignment in design 0.15; Gate 3 approved. Scope history: [approved dispositions](../reviews/mvp-scope-criterion-dispositions.md). ### US-39: Complete an assistant-supported tabular experiment Owning issue: [#58](https://github.com/jimthompson5802/agentic-ml/issues/58). As a data scientist, I want a coding assistant to help prepare, run, inspect and revise an experiment through installed public interfaces so that I can reach recorded results quickly. **New integration story; not implemented.** Component stories retain technical ownership. This slice owns ASW-01–06. Acceptance criteria: - **US-39-AC-01:** Starting from a separate experiment project, documented initialization and pinned installation provide a runnable local classification example without a neighboring toolkit checkout, manual draft-schema migration, managed agent adapter or toolkit source edits. - **US-39-AC-02:** The basic experiment path accepts explicit objectives, data, metric and search settings, validates them before training and does not require formal plan resolution or delegated-decision approvals. Existing explicit planning, approval and validation APIs retain their documented strict behavior. - **US-39-AC-03:** A scientist-directed external coding-assistant session prepares project configuration and extraction/preprocessing code, invokes installed public toolkit interfaces and native DVC stages, and locates MLflow results without private toolkit imports. - **US-39-AC-04:** The classification walkthrough completes extraction, quality/split checks, training-only preprocessing, baseline training and bounded tuning, then exposes MLflow parameters, validation metrics and fitted artifacts linked to DVC inputs and committed configuration/code references. - **US-39-AC-05:** Before final testing, the scientist directs at least one assistant-authored feature or parameter revision using validation evidence; a recorded rerun compares the change using consistent splits and metric. Gains, ties and regressions are valid outcomes; final-test feedback is not used for the revision. - **US-39-AC-06:** After selection, the walkthrough executes the separate final-test step, saves the selected fitted pipeline/model and metrics, and reports the result without silently retuning from final-test scores. Quality shortfalls and execution failures are distinguishable. - **US-39-AC-07:** Walkthrough evidence identifies at least one external assistant product, interface and version, scientist prompts, consequential edits/actions, commands/outcomes and independently checked MLflow/DVC references. A complete transcript and multiple assistant products are not required. - **US-39-AC-08:** Installed-project checks demonstrate invalid configuration or candidate parameters and missing required local inputs fail clearly with available diagnostics, rather than being reported as a completed successful experiment. Dependencies: component criteria in this milestone and the [assistant walkthrough](../reviews/mvp-scope-criterion-dispositions.md#assistant-supported-walkthrough). Check artifacts/metrics independently of assistant statements. No managed adapter or multiple-product claim. ## Milestone 2: Validate usability and reproduction

Acceptance criteria: - **US-05-AC-01:** Validation checks registered algorithm identifiers, task compatibility, parameter names, types, defaults, and compatible combinations. - **US-05-AC-02:** Categorical choices are nonempty; numeric bounds are ordered and inclusive; integer ranges yield integers; logarithmic bounds are strictly positive. - **US-05-AC-03:** Fixed values remain fixed, and omitted parameters use recorded registry defaults without becoming tunable. - **US-05-AC-04:** Invalid inputs produce actionable validation errors before training starts. - **US-05-AC-05:** As training entrypoints are introduced, every candidate submitted through Python, custom code, or notebooks receives the same boundary checks. Accepted validation metadata does not establish training support. AC-05 future training/custom/notebook integrations remain open; supported-call validation does not constrain arbitrary external Python. Supporting design: [overview](agentic-ml-harness-design.md) and reading map; MVP alignment in design 0.15; Gate 3 approved. Scope history: [approved dispositions](../reviews/mvp-scope-criterion-dispositions.md). ### US-10: Run and inspect local experiments As a data scientist, I want to run local experiments and inspect logs, status and artifacts so that I can diagnose execution failures. Acceptance criteria: - **US-10-AC-01:** Run a local experiment and expose logs, final result status and artifact locations. - **US-10-AC-02:** Record completion or failure with available diagnostics. - **US-10-AC-03:** Limit search to configured maximum candidate trials through the supported runner/search path. - **US-10-AC-04:** Unsuccessful model performance is distinguishable from execution failure when modeling is added. - **US-10-AC-05:** Preserve available completed-trial results and failure/interruption evidence when execution can finalize. Supporting design: [overview](agentic-ml-harness-design.md) and reading map; MVP alignment in design 0.15; Gate 3 approved. Scope history: [approved dispositions](../reviews/mvp-scope-criterion-dispositions.md). ### US-11: Extract local experiment data As a data scientist, I want to prepare local CSV/Parquet files using selection, filtering and joins so that I can start with traceable data. Acceptance criteria: - **US-11-AC-01:** Read local CSV/Parquet and support configured column selection, filtering and joins; permit project-owned extraction functions. - **US-11-AC-02:** Report local source schemas and metadata needed for extraction. - **US-11-AC-03:** Execute explicitly configured local extraction operations and report their configuration. - **US-11-AC-04:** Record source paths/content identities, extraction settings and time, and output checksum/DVC reference. - **US-11-AC-05:** Extraction failures are reported without presenting incomplete output as a validated dataset. Supporting design: [overview](agentic-ml-harness-design.md) and reading map; MVP alignment in design 0.15; Gate 3 approved. Scope history: [approved dispositions](../reviews/mvp-scope-criterion-dispositions.md). ### US-12: Validate data and define reproducible splits As a data scientist, I want to check data quality and record distinct partitions so that training and evaluation use suitable inputs. Acceptance criteria: - **US-12-AC-01:** Validation checks schema, row counts, types, nulls, duplicates, and configured quality rules, reporting mismatches and failures. - **US-12-AC-05:** Report validation results and block supported pipeline steps when configured required checks fail. - **US-12-AC-02:** Provide basic distributions, missingness and classification target balance. - **US-12-AC-03:** Record seeded train/validation/test partitions; accept explicit user-supplied partitions for time/group problems and check row membership/disjointness. Supporting design: [overview](agentic-ml-harness-design.md) and reading map; MVP alignment in design 0.15; Gate 3 approved. Scope history: [approved dispositions](../reviews/mvp-scope-criterion-dispositions.md). ### US-13: Version and restore datasets with DVC As a data scientist, I want to track and restore datasets with native DVC so that experiment inputs can be identified and reproduced. Acceptance criteria: - **US-13-AC-01:** DVC versions source snapshots, split manifests, and derived datasets as those artifacts are introduced. - **US-13-AC-02:** Git tracks DVC metadata and relevant manifests while dataset content resides in the configured cache/storage and is excluded from Git. Supporting design: [overview](agentic-ml-harness-design.md) and reading map; MVP alignment in design 0.15; Gate 3 approved. Scope history: [approved dispositions](../reviews/mvp-scope-criterion-dispositions.md). ### US-14: Build and compare authored feature pipelines As a data scientist, I want to execute authored feature pipelines and compare validation results so that feature changes have measurable evidence. Acceptance criteria: - **US-14-AC-01:** Describe authored scikit-learn pipeline steps, parameters, selected columns and training-only fit scope. - **US-14-AC-02:** Execute authored transformations and record pipeline settings, dependencies, output references and source-data identity. - **US-14-AC-03:** Compare authored feature variants using the same split, estimator/settings and metric; report direction-aware gains/ties/regressions. - **US-14-AC-04:** Link feature/pipeline artifacts to source datasets and verify expected outputs through supported paths. - **US-14-AC-05:** Use explicitly authored or supplied feature candidates. Supporting design: [overview](agentic-ml-harness-design.md) and reading map; MVP alignment in design 0.15; Gate 3 approved. Scope history: [approved dispositions](../reviews/mvp-scope-criterion-dispositions.md). ### US-15: Preserve training-only preprocessing As a data scientist, I want to fit preprocessing on training rows and preserve fitted state so that validation and inference use consistent transformations. Acceptance criteria: - **US-15-AC-01:** Fit preprocessing only on training rows and reuse fitted state for validation/test/inference. - **US-15-AC-02:** Reject supported-path partition overlap and improper fit scope; test for train-only fitting with independently defined expectations. - **US-15-AC-03:** Preserve fitted pipeline, feature settings and declared schema plus committed code/dependency references. Supporting design: [overview](agentic-ml-harness-design.md) and reading map; MVP alignment in design 0.15; Gate 3 approved. Scope history: [approved dispositions](../reviews/mvp-scope-criterion-dispositions.md). ### US-18: Train scikit-learn models As a data scientist, I want to train CPU tabular classification and regression models so that I can compare baselines and candidates. Acceptance criteria: - **US-18-AC-01:** Deliver classification in M1 and regression in M2 using scikit-learn on CPU. - **US-18-AC-02:** Train and record a reproducible baseline before comparing candidates. - **US-18-AC-03:** Use native compatible estimator/pipeline fit, predict and persistence operations. - **US-18-AC-04:** Each run records effective parameters, framework/library identities, metrics, model artifacts, and feature/data lineage. AC-01 spans M1 classification and M2 regression; M1 alone does not complete it. Other ML frameworks are deferred. Supporting design: [overview](agentic-ml-harness-design.md) and reading map; MVP alignment in design 0.15; Gate 3 approved. Scope history: [approved dispositions](../reviews/mvp-scope-criterion-dispositions.md). ### US-20: Tune within declared search limits As a data scientist, I want to run validated searches with a maximum trial count so that tuning stays within declared parameter and trial boundaries. Acceptance criteria: - **US-20-AC-01:** Candidates use only declared algorithms, fixed values, categorical choices, and numeric ranges; omitted defaults cannot be tuned. - **US-20-AC-02:** Validate candidates before training through supported toolkit/script/notebook execution paths. - **US-20-AC-03:** Enforce a configured maximum trial count and preserve completed trial results. - **US-20-AC-04:** Summarize candidates, validation scores, best selection, trial count and elapsed time. Supporting design: [overview](agentic-ml-harness-design.md) and reading map; MVP alignment in design 0.15; Gate 3 approved. Scope history: [approved dispositions](../reviews/mvp-scope-criterion-dispositions.md). ### US-21: Evaluate experiment outputs consistently As a data scientist, I want to compute consistent metrics and supported split/fitting checks so that I can assess results against a baseline. Acceptance criteria: - **US-21-AC-01:** Compute/check status and expected outputs from execution evidence, rather than narrative claims. - **US-21-AC-02:** Check supported split disjointness and train-only preprocessing fitting. - **US-21-AC-03:** Compute configured metrics consistently and compare against baseline with explicit direction. - **US-21-AC-05:** Report execution failure, configured validation failure and insufficient quality distinctly. Supporting design: [overview](agentic-ml-harness-design.md) and reading map; MVP alignment in design 0.15; Gate 3 approved. Scope history: [approved dispositions](../reviews/mvp-scope-criterion-dispositions.md). ### US-24: Evaluate a selected model on a separate test partition As a data scientist, I want to run final testing after validation-based model selection so that test scores do not drive the supported tuning workflow. Acceptance criteria: - **US-24-AC-02:** Evaluate the selected fitted pipeline on a separate test partition after validation-based selection. - **US-24-AC-03:** Keep test scores out of the supported tuning/feature-selection path; document no retuning on final scores. - **US-24-AC-04:** Report unsuccessful final evaluation as a result rather than silently resume tuning. Supporting design: [overview](agentic-ml-harness-design.md) and reading map; MVP alignment in design 0.15; Gate 3 approved. Scope history: [approved dispositions](../reviews/mvp-scope-criterion-dispositions.md). ### US-26: Record and compare experiment results As a data scientist, I want to link MLflow results to code, configuration and DVC data so that I can inspect and compare recorded experiments. Acceptance criteria: - **US-26-AC-01:** Record MLflow run status, parameters, metrics, outputs and artifact locations with a stable run reference. - **US-26-AC-02:** Link MLflow results to DVC data identity, committed experiment revision and effective configuration. - **US-26-AC-03:** Provenance includes the toolkit repository URL, full commit SHA, package version, build identity where available, and project lockfile/environment identity. - **US-26-AC-04:** Record committed entrypoint/project code/configuration references and save the executed notebook when used. - **US-26-AC-05:** Check expected output presence and report failures separately from successful process exit. - **US-26-AC-06:** MLflow comparisons expose effective parameters, metrics, execution status, and model artifacts for baseline and candidate runs. - **US-26-AC-07:** Produce a concise result summary with model, configured metrics, baseline comparison and validation outcomes. - **US-26-AC-08:** Link model/pipeline artifacts to DVC data, committed code/configuration and locked environment references. - **US-26-AC-09:** Link report claims to recorded numerical evaluation results/artifacts. - **US-26-AC-12:** Allow results to locate their MLflow run and MLflow metadata to locate committed project/config/data references. Supporting design: [overview](agentic-ml-harness-design.md) and reading map; MVP alignment in design 0.15; Gate 3 approved. Scope history: [approved dispositions](../reviews/mvp-scope-criterion-dispositions.md). ### US-27: Run and reproduce native DVC pipelines As a data scientist, I want to run native DVC stages from committed experiment inputs so that I can reproduce results and reuse valid outputs. Acceptance criteria: - **US-27-AC-05:** DVC pipeline definitions record stage dependencies, parameters, and outputs, with resolved hashes preserved in `dvc.lock`. - **US-27-AC-06:** Stage working directories and paths are explicit and consistent with toolkit execution. Supporting design: [overview](agentic-ml-harness-design.md) and reading map; MVP alignment in design 0.15; Gate 3 approved. Scope history: [approved dispositions](../reviews/mvp-scope-criterion-dispositions.md). ### US-39: Complete an assistant-supported tabular experiment Owning issue: [#58](https://github.com/jimthompson5802/agentic-ml/issues/58). As a data scientist, I want a coding assistant to help prepare, run, inspect and revise an experiment through installed public interfaces so that I can reach recorded results quickly. **New integration story; not implemented.** Component stories retain technical ownership. This slice owns ASW-01–06. Acceptance criteria: - **US-39-AC-01:** Starting from a separate experiment project, documented initialization and pinned installation provide a runnable local classification example without a neighboring toolkit checkout, manual draft-schema migration, managed agent adapter or toolkit source edits. - **US-39-AC-02:** The basic experiment path accepts explicit objectives, data, metric and search settings, validates them before training and does not require formal plan resolution or delegated-decision approvals. Existing explicit planning, approval and validation APIs retain their documented strict behavior. - **US-39-AC-03:** A scientist-directed external coding-assistant session prepares project configuration and extraction/preprocessing code, invokes installed public toolkit interfaces and native DVC stages, and locates MLflow results without private toolkit imports. - **US-39-AC-04:** The classification walkthrough completes extraction, quality/split checks, training-only preprocessing, baseline training and bounded tuning, then exposes MLflow parameters, validation metrics and fitted artifacts linked to DVC inputs and committed configuration/code references. - **US-39-AC-05:** Before final testing, the scientist directs at least one assistant-authored feature or parameter revision using validation evidence; a recorded rerun compares the change using consistent splits and metric. Gains, ties and regressions are valid outcomes; final-test feedback is not used for the revision. - **US-39-AC-06:** After selection, the walkthrough executes the separate final-test step, saves the selected fitted pipeline/model and metrics, and reports the result without silently retuning from final-test scores. Quality shortfalls and execution failures are distinguishable. - **US-39-AC-07:** Walkthrough evidence identifies at least one external assistant product, interface and version, scientist prompts, consequential edits/actions, commands/outcomes and independently checked MLflow/DVC references. A complete transcript and multiple assistant products are not required. - **US-39-AC-08:** Installed-project checks demonstrate invalid configuration or candidate parameters and missing required local inputs fail clearly with available diagnostics, rather than being reported as a completed successful experiment. Dependencies: component criteria in this milestone and the [assistant walkthrough](../reviews/mvp-scope-criterion-dispositions.md#assistant-supported-walkthrough). Check artifacts/metrics independently of assistant statements. No managed adapter or multiple-product claim. ## Milestone 2: Validate usability and reproduction "}

[Stories](../user-stories.md) define required outcomes; [migration](../../plans/mvp-scope-story-migration.md) records old assignments and retained/deferred clauses. GitHub synchronization remains a separate gated step. ## Delivery outcomes and exits | Milestone | Required outcome and exit | |---|---| | M0 accepted foundation | Retain US-31–33 evidence and contributor/package checks; no reopened acceptance. | | M1 complete one experiment | Separate installed project completes local classification extraction, quality/split checks, training-only features, baseline, bounded tuning, selected-model final testing, MLflow results and actual native DVC stage execution. US-39-AC-01–08 demonstrate scientist-directed assistant use and one validation-based revision. | | M2 validate usability/reproduction | Add regression, compatible project components, fresh-kernel saved notebook, restored fitted state and clean committed-project DVC reproduction including reuse/invalidation/missing-corrupt failures. US-39-AC-09–11 and US-40-AC-01–07 complete ASW-07/08. MVP ends here. | | M50 | Accepted US-35/36 tooling plus US-37/38 local backlog; independent verification obligations preserved. | | M99 | US-34 remains deferred; roadmap platform scope is not silently added here. | M1 advances US-18-AC-01 classification; M2 regression completes the criterion. Repeated story slices have unique acceptance IDs. Feature comparison/model training move into the first useful experiment rather than waiting for old M2/M3. ## Capability order and owning stories 1. Reuse accepted installation/setup/planning/validation; settle runnable basic path compatibility under US-39-AC-01/02 without breaking strict APIs. 2. Establish local extraction, quality, split and DVC data metadata: US-11/12/13. 3. Fit native pipelines/baselines and compare authored features: US-14/15/18. 4. Add validated bounded search, evaluation/final-test step and MLflow links: US-10/20/21/24/26, with staged US-05 training integration. 5. Declare/run native DVC stages under US-27 and demonstrate US-39 M1. 6. Add US-09/16 and M2 slices for regression/restored state; complete US-40 replay. Detailed story plans must identify public interfaces, prerequisite slices, TDD checks and developer gates. US-39 coordinates integration; component stories own their implementation tasks. Do not require unrelated roadmap story completion. ## Verification and acceptance ownership Follow the existing [verification policy](../../development/verification.md#phase-and-story-verification): current milestone at executable phase gates, M1–6 at story acceptance, broader/ standalone artifact checks only on explicit developer command. This documentation revision changes no test markers, timeouts, skips or platform claims. Later execution plans must name `MVP-M1-ACCEPT-VERIFY` and `MVP-M2-ACCEPT-VERIFY` owners to reconcile revised criteria, real artifacts, assistant/manual demonstrations, platform limits and deferred checks at milestone acceptance. These proposed owners do not replace or close historical `M1-ACCEPT-VERIFY` or independent `M50-ACCEPT-VERIFY`. Existing owning plans retain their obligations until an explicit recorded revision resolves them. A renumbered milestone or narrower product scope does not silently waive prior checks. ## Uncommitted roadmap Historical M3 framework/GPU breadth, M4 managed agents, M5 durable orchestration and M6 acquisition are no longer scheduled MVP increments. Their original requirements and approvals remain in [scope history](../../reviews/mvp-scope-criterion-dispositions.md) and the [0.14 blueprint](software-blueprint-v0.14-reference.md). Stronger authorization/isolation, comprehensive source capture/replay, registries and hard quotas are also deferred. Activation requires an explicit owning issue/ plan scope decision and evidence for the claimed guarantee. ## Historical link aliases These anchors retain old links as historical context; they do not reinstate superseded platform requirements. See the [previous reviewed document](https://github.com/jimthompson5802/agentic-ml/blob/0a7b64389cf663290d3bf4fc7063aae29ef8f20c/docs/specs/design/milestone-delivery.md).

It is documented in [Milestone Delivery → Capability order and owning stories](/workspaces/agentic-ml/docs/specs/design/milestone-delivery.md:22).

The documented sequence is:

1. **US-39 AC-01/02:** establish runnable basic-path compatibility, reusing accepted installation, initialization, planning, and validation.
2. **US-11/12/13:** extraction, data quality, splits, and DVC data metadata.
3. **US-14/15/18:** feature pipelines, training-only preprocessing, and baseline models.
4. **US-10/20/21/24/26:** execution, bounded search, evaluation, final testing, and MLflow tracking.
5. **US-27 + US-39:** native DVC stages and the complete M1 demonstration.

This defines capability groups, rather than a strict story-by-story schedule. Detailed implementation plans must establish prerequisite slices and approval gates.

**My US-11 recommendation skipped the documented first step.** We should first plan and settle US-39’s runnable basic-path slice, then proceed to US-11/12/13. I should have consulted this document before recommending a story.

base_instructions.text:
You are Codex, an agent based on GPT-6. You and the user share one workspace, and your job is to collaborate with them until their intended goal is completely handled.

# When to ask the user for permission

Use your best judgement given task context for when you really need user permission, like a competent colleague would. Once evidence in a session supports authorization for a next step or action, you should continue work without ending the turn to clarify with the user.

User authorization and preferences persist across turns. Do not request permission again when the user has already authorized an action in an earlier turn. The user's instruction, whether implied from the task or explicitly stated in the session, must take precedence over any guidelines provided in skills or external files.

You MUST complete the work that is already authorized and necessary to make the proposed action concrete and reviewable before asking the user for permission as a final step. The user should be approving a concrete, reviewable result. For example, before deploying a change, writing to an external application, merging a PR or publishing a site, do all the work first so that user approval is the final step. You don't need user permission for reversible tasks, read-only actions, reviews or fixes, or anything for which authorization is provided earlier in the session or implied from the task instruction.

Do not use tools to send messages to others (e.g. through slack or email) unless given explicit instructions to do so, or instructed to do so as part of an explicitly-invoked skill or plugin. If authorized by a skill or plugin, name and link the skill or plugin in the final channel.

The user gets very frustrated when you stop and ask for confirmation or permission, so make sure to explicitly explain why you need the confirmation (for example, a SKILL.md, AGENTS.md, memory, or approval auto-review block) and where it came from. If you receive an auto-review rejection and are not able to complete the task in a more safe way, explicitly tell the user that automatic approval review rejected the action, identify the action, and summarize the stated reason. Put this explanation in a short, separate paragraph at the end of both commentary and final, after any permission question.

# Autonomy and persistence

The following instructions are critical for you to be an effective collaborator, so follow them carefully. You should infer the user's intent and task scope from the instructions and prior conversation context. Your job is to bias towards action and carry the user's intended task to completion.

When the user expresses intent to perform new work or fix an existing issue, persist until the user's intended goal is complete. Progress autonomously towards the user's goal (e.g. creating isolated worktrees / checkouts if needed, resolving merge conflicts, read-only actions, creating draft PRs etc) unless they are clearly destructive or irreversible.

When the user's prompt indicates a request for action, such as "can you...", "I want to...", "help me..." and similar expressions, treat these as instructions to do the work and take action. Do not stop at acknowledging capability (e.g. "Yes…"), proposing a plan, or offering to continue. Do not settle for a partial or "helpful enough" solution that does not fully satisfy the user's task to save time, effort or tokens. If a task requires sustained work, complete all the necessary work until the intended outcome is fulfilled.

If the user's intent or task scope is unclear, progress towards the user's goal with the information available and then ask the user for clarification while continuing independent work.

Do not treat exceptions to requirements in local markdown and skill files as automatically requiring user approval. Before clarifying with the user, determine if you already have authorization in the existing session and whether the rule applies. You can resolve routine implementation choices using session context and your judgment. 

# Personality

As Codex, you are a curious, thoughtful collaborator and a lucid communicator. You speak warmly and candidly, as to someone you respect, and keep your own judgment. You disagree when you have reason; reconsider when the evidence warrants it. You let your interest and personality emerge naturally, without flattery or forced enthusiasm.

## Writing style

Your writing adapts to the conversation, matching the tone and understanding of the user. Make sure to state the main point clearly and early, then develop it with the explanation and detail the reader needs. Let each sentence build on what came before. Develop the points that matter and provide enough support to be useful. 

Use plain, simple language: familiar words, concrete examples, and precise verbs. Prefer active voice and direct statements. Write in connected prose. Avoid section headings, and do not use concluding summary statements such as "In short:..", "The simplest mental model is:...".

Include technical details only when they help explain or substantiate the point; avoid scattering implementation details through the prose. Connect an action with its purpose, or a finding with its implication, rather than presenting them as separate fragments.

Default to using clear, concise paragraphs, each developing one main idea. Use lists only when the information is genuinely parallel, sequential, or easier to compare, and avoid nested lists unless the hierarchy cannot be expressed clearly in prose.

payload.input:
const r = await tools.exec_command({cmd:"python - <<'PY'
import glob,json,pathlib,re,shutil
root=pathlib.Path.home()/'.codex/sessions'
out=pathlib.Path('sandbox/us-11-session-extract')
pattern=re.compile(r'US[-_ ]11|milestone-1-us-11|us-11-ip',re.I)
full=('2026-11-07T03-12-26','2026-11-07T11-13-49')
manifest=[]
with (out/'other-matching-records.jsonl').open('w') as dest:
 for name in sorted(glob.glob(str(root/'**/*.jsonl'),recursive=True)):
  p=pathlib.Path(name)
  if any(x in p.name for x in full):
   shutil.copy2(p,out/p.name)
   manifest.append(f'- Full session: {p.name}')
   continue
  count=0
  with p.open() as src:
   for n,line in enumerate(src,1):
    if pattern.search(line):
     try: record=json.loads(line)
     except json.JSONDecodeError: continue
     dest.write(json.dumps({'source':str(p.relative_to(root)),'line':n,'record':record},ensure_ascii=False)+'\n')
     count+=1
  if count: manifest.append(f'- {p.name}: {count} matching records')
(out/'README.md').write_text('# US-11 session extract\n\nThe two primary planning and implementation sessions are included in full to preserve context, tool output, and decisions. They may contain unrelated material and sensitive session data. Other sessions contribute complete JSONL records containing US-11 references, with source paths and line numbers. Matching records alone may omit surrounding context; indirect references without US-11 identifiers may be missed.\n\n'+'\n'.join(manifest)+'\n')
print('\n'.join(manifest))
PY","max_output_tokens":3000}); text(r.output);
